title: The pre-commit hook's export flush is not covered by its own test suite
description:
## Outcome

Both halves of the pre-commit hook are guarded. Deleting `br sync --flush-only` from
`.githooks/pre-commit` turns a case in `scripts/test_beads_hook.sh` red, naming the bead that
failed to reach the commit, exactly as deleting the staging loop already does.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a clone of this repository, edit `.githooks/pre-commit` and replace `br sync --flush-only`
   with a no-op. **Commit the edit** — the suite clones from `HEAD`, so a working-tree change is
   invisible to it and the mutation silently proves nothing.
2. `bash scripts/test_beads_hook.sh`.
3. `beads-hook tests: 12 passed, 0 failed`. The hook's flush is gone and nothing notices.

For contrast, the same procedure applied to the staging loop (`git add -f -- "$f"`) turns four
cases red: `s1: .beads dirty after the commit`, `s1: bead <id> is NOT in the committed
issues.jsonl`, `s2: worktree .beads dirty after the commit`, and `s2: bead <id> missing from the
worktree commit`. That half is properly guarded; this one is not.

## Context

Measured 2026-08-26 while reviewing `bd-imt` before merging it. The hook is correct and the bead
is not being reopened: its outcome, a locally created bead reaching the commit, is proven by the
staging half. What is missing is coverage of the other half.

The reason the flush looks redundant is that `br` auto-flushes the JSONL export on every
mutation, so by the time the hook runs the file is already current on disk and only the staging
is left to do. Every scenario the suite builds goes through an ordinary `br create`, so every
scenario arrives in that state.

**The flush is not dead code, and today proved it.** A `br` mutation during this run answered:

> `Warning: Mutation succeeded, but automatic JSONL export failed. Fix the export problem, run
> br sync --flush-only, then commit the updated .beads/issues.jsonl.`
> `Error: I/O error: Quota exceeded (os error 122)`

The cause was `/tmp` being full, which `br` writes its export through. In that state the
database holds the bead, the export on disk does not, and the hook's flush is the only thing
between that and a commit whose tracker snapshot silently omits a bead. `br --no-auto-flush`
reaches the same state deliberately. So the untested half covers the case the hook was built
for, and the tested half covers the easy one.

This is the shape worth naming rather than the specific line: a suite whose scenarios all reach
the subject through the same happy path measures one mechanism and reports on two.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A scenario leaves the export **stale on disk while the database is ahead** — through
      `br --no-auto-flush`, or by writing a bead and then reverting the export file — and then
      commits.
- [ ] With the hook intact, that scenario passes: the committed `issues.jsonl` contains the bead.
- [ ] With `br sync --flush-only` removed from the hook and the removal **committed**, that
      scenario fails, and the failure names the bead that did not reach the commit.
- [ ] The test file states, where the new scenario is built, why an ordinary `br create` cannot
      exercise this path — otherwise the next reader simplifies it back into the happy path.
- [ ] `scripts/test_beads_hook.sh` still passes in full, and its count goes up by the number of
      cases added.
- [ ] Done when: each of the hook's two mechanisms has at least one case that goes red when that
      mechanism alone is deleted.

## Tests

- **Integration (shell), the deliverable itself:** one new scenario in
  `scripts/test_beads_hook.sh` driving a stale-export commit in the scratch clone.
- **Mutation, before it is trusted:** delete `br sync --flush-only`, commit the deletion, run
  the suite, and confirm the new case is the one that fails. A mutation left uncommitted is
  invisible to this suite and proves nothing.

## Blast radius

`scripts/test_beads_hook.sh` only. The hook itself is correct and is not edited; if the new
scenario turns out to need a hook change, that is a different bead and should be said out loud
rather than folded in here.
close_reason: verified at 524e26f8. Mutation independently re-run by the orchestrator, committed so the suite's scratch clone can see it: removing 'br sync --flush-only' from the pre-commit hook now turns scenario 4 red naming the bead that never reached the committed JSONL. Before this change the same mutation left all 12 cases green, which is the gap this bead closed. 15/15 with the hook intact. PR #24 merged.

title: assign --clear releases a claim whose durable record is gone, or the claim rolls back
description:
## Outcome

A bead claim created by `ntm assign` can always be released through ntm: either the atomic coordinator rolls its claim back when prompt delivery fails, or `ntm assign --clear <bead>` releases the underlying br claim even when the durable assignment record is already gone - so the documented recovery command never answers "assignment not found or already completed" while the claim it exists to clear still stands.

## Context

Measured on the agent-usage-book reference run, 2026-08-30 (survey run-log 6db7d42b in llm-workflow): two dispatches failed after the atomic claim landed. One strand (aub-23p5) cleared normally via `ntm assign --clear`. The other (aub-xus.1) answered "Cleared 0 of 1 bead assignments: ✗ aub-xus.1: assignment not found or already completed" while the br claim stood untouched (in_progress, assignee EmeraldCat) - the durable record's lifetime was shorter than the claim's, and the operator had to release br-side by hand. Traced 2026-08-31: `runDirectPaneAssignment` (internal/cli/assign.go:5747) drives `AtomicCoordinator.Execute` (internal/assignment/atomic.go:712) via the claim port wired at assign.go:3110-3157; the `--clear` path looks a bead up only in `store.GetAll()` (assign.go:4310-4321), prints exactly that message when no record exists (assign.go:4321), and never reaches `releaseBeadClaimForAssignment` (assign.go:4216, inside `clearStoredAssignmentIfStatus`, assign.go:4151). So a claim whose store record is absent is unreleasable through ntm by construction. The closed bd-htr is a different symptom (same-intent replay refused with PANE_BUSY over a record that exists); this is the record-absent case. Downstream, llm-workflow's dispatcher is growing an automatic two-step release (lw-qunr) whose fallback is a raw br write precisely because of this gap - closing it here lets that fallback stay the exception.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drive an `ntm assign` whose atomic claim lands but whose prompt delivery fails (the measured trigger was delivery into a pane still in its boot window), and arrange for the durable assignment record to be gone (expired or dropped) while the br claim stands.
2. Run the printed recovery: `ntm assign <session> --clear <bead>`.
3. Observe "✗ <bead>: assignment not found or already completed", exit without releasing; `br show <bead>` still shows the claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a dispatch failure after the claim landed, either the coordinator releases its own claim before returning (rollback), or the failure output states the claim is intentionally kept and `--clear` is guaranteed to work on it - one of the two, decided and documented in the command's help.
- [ ] `--clear` on a bead with no durable record but a standing br claim created by ntm releases that claim (reusing `releaseBeadClaimForAssignment`) instead of reporting "not found", and says which path released it.
- [ ] `--clear` on a bead with no record and no ntm-created claim still reports not-found and touches nothing (another actor's claim is never released).
- [ ] Done when: the reproduction above ends with the bead back in `br ready --unassigned` via ntm alone, and the other-actor case is proven untouched in the same test run.

## Tests

- Unit (Go, coordinator/clear paths): store-record-absent with own claim releases; store-record-absent with foreign claim refuses; record-present path unchanged.
- Integration: the reproduction, scripted against a scratch tracker and a throwaway pane.

## Blast radius

Confined to internal/cli/assign.go (the `--clear` lookup and release paths, ~4151-4321) and, if rollback is the chosen half, the failure branch of internal/assignment/atomic.go's Execute plus its ports; their tests. No change to the success path's claim semantics.
close_reason: assign --clear falls back to the live tracker when the durable record is gone: releases only an assignee matching ntm's stable actor shape (<base>/ntm-<12hex>), compare-and-set on the observed actor, released_via reported; dispatch-failure keeps the claim deliberately and names --clear as recovery; PR 43 merged; go test ./internal/assignment + cli Clear tests green run by orchestrator; implemented by glm-5.3-flash-max-k2 on attempt 3 (k3 session quota, then proxy restart)

title: ntm bind writes a key tmux refuses: validation admits a leading dash and a failed live bind does not stop the config write
description:
## Outcome

`ntm bind` cannot write a line into a user's `~/.tmux.conf` that tmux refuses to parse. A key that
tmux would read as a flag is rejected before anything is written, and a live `bind-key` that fails
stops the config write instead of being downgraded to a warning. A user who mistypes an invocation
gets an error and an unchanged config, not a tmux that complains on every start.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `ntm bind --key --help` (cobra assigns `--help` as the value of `--key`).
2. `ntm` accepts it, prints a warning that it could not bind in the current session, and appends to
   `~/.tmux.conf`:

        # NTM Command Palette (added by 'ntm bind')
        bind-key -n --help display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% "ntm palette"

3. Start tmux, or run `tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf`:

        /home/gabriel/.tmux.conf:3: command bind-key: invalid flag --

Observed on a real machine 2026-08-24. The file was written on 2026-08-15 15:53 and every tmux
start in the nine days between reported the error; the binding never worked, and nothing in `ntm`
ever said so again after the first run.

## Context

Two independent gaps combine, and the second is the one that makes it permanent.

**The validation admits a leading dash.** `validKeyRegex` (`internal/cli/bind.go:19`) is
`^[a-zA-Z0-9\-\^]+$`, and its comment says it exists "to validate tmux key bindings (alphanumeric,
-, ^ for Ctrl)". The `-` is there for key names like `C-a`, but the anchor allows it in first
position, so `--help` — six characters all inside the allowed set — passes the check at
`bind.go:53`. Every `--flag` a user could plausibly mistype is made of allowed characters, so this
is not a narrow edge case: the guard is blind to exactly the class of value that breaks tmux.

**The program already had the evidence and discarded it.** When run inside tmux, `setupBinding`
first applies the binding to the live server (`bind.go:89`), which fails for a bad key. That
failure is printed as a warning and execution continues to the config write (`bind.go:84`, then the
append at `bind.go:136`). So the one check that would have caught this — asking tmux whether it
accepts the key — is performed, fails, and is ignored. The user is left with a warning about the
current session and a permanent line in their config.

The default key is `F6` (`bind.go:70`), so the intended content of that line is known and the
damage is a single token.

`--overlay` takes the same path with a default of `F12`, and `--unbind` and `--show` route through
`removeBinding` and `showBinding` with the same unvalidated key, so a fix belongs at the validation
and the write, not in one branch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ntm bind --key --help` exits non-zero, writes nothing to `~/.tmux.conf`, and its error names
      the rejected value
- [ ] A key beginning with `-` is rejected. `C-a`, `M-Left`, `F6` and `^A` are still accepted — the
      fix restricts the first character, it does not remove `-` from the alphabet
- [ ] When `ntm` is running inside tmux and the live `bind-key` fails, the config file is not
      modified. Today that failure is a warning and the write proceeds
- [ ] The same guard covers `--overlay`, `--unbind` and `--show`, which share the key argument
- [ ] After a successful `ntm bind`, the written line is proven to parse — `tmux source-file` on the
      resulting file succeeds, asserted rather than assumed
- [ ] An existing `~/.tmux.conf` already holding a broken line is not silently rewritten by this
      change: repairing it is the user's action, and the bead does not grant `ntm` the right to edit
      lines it did not just write
- [ ] Done when: no invocation of `ntm bind`, valid or mistyped, can leave a `~/.tmux.conf` that
      `tmux source-file` rejects.

## Tests

- **Unit test** — table-driven over the key validator: `--help`, `-k`, `--overlay` and a bare `-`
  are rejected; `F6`, `F12`, `C-a`, `M-Left`, `^A` and `q` are accepted. Assert the rejection
  message names the value.
- **Unit test** — `setupBinding` with a live-bind failure injected: assert the config file is
  byte-identical afterwards. This is the branch that turned a typo into nine days of errors, and it
  is currently a warning with no coverage.
- **Unit test** — `--overlay`, `--unbind` and `--show` with a dash-leading key: each rejects, none
  writes.
- **Golden test** — the file `ntm bind` produces for the default key, checked into testdata and
  fed through `tmux source-file` in a test that skips when no tmux binary is present. The bead
  exists because nobody ever checked that the generated line parses.

Every assertion must be driven red on purpose. A validator test that passes against the current
regex is testing the alphabet, not this bead.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/bind.go` — the regex at `:19`, its use at `:53`, and the ordering of the live bind at
`:89` against the config append at `:136` — plus `internal/cli/bind_test.go` and one testdata file.
No other command reads `validKeyRegex`, the tmux config format is not otherwise touched, and the
palette and overlay commands themselves are unchanged.

## Recovery path

Validation and control flow in one file, with no persisted state of its own, so reverting the
commit restores the previous behaviour. A `~/.tmux.conf` already carrying a broken line is repaired
by hand — replacing the bad token with `F6` restores the intended binding, which is what was done on
the machine where this was found.
close_reason: Implemented in 8e2fbe60. validKeyRegex anchors the first character to a letter, digit or ^ so a dash-leading value is rejected before anything is written, and a failed live bind-key now returns an error instead of warning and writing the config anyway; both palette and overlay paths, covering --unbind and --show. Adds a golden test that feeds the generated default-key config through 'tmux source-file' on an isolated -L socket. Verified by mutation: restoring the old regex turns four TestValidateKey rows and all four TestBindRejectsDashLeadingKeyAcrossModes rows red, and restoring warn-and-continue turns TestSetupBindingLiveBindFailureDoesNotWriteConfig red. internal/cli green.

title: Classify a live provider modal as its own state, not error
description:
## Outcome

A pane sitting on a live provider modal (quota exhaustion, model-switch confirmation, upgrade prompt) is classified as its own actionable state instead of `error`, so consumers that act on `error` (restart management, SafeToDispatch, wait) neither restart a pane that is merely waiting for an operator decision nor treat it as crashed - and the state a tender sees names the actual situation: an armed modal one keystroke from a silent model downgrade.

## Context

Measured on the agent-usage-book reference run, 2026-08-31 (survey run-log 6db7d42b in llm-workflow): pane 6 (codex) sat on "You've hit your usage limit. Upgrade to Pro ( 1. Switch to... Fast and affordable ... Press enter to confirm" - a quota modal with the model-switch option armed on Enter. `ntm activity` reported the pane state as ERROR, sniffed from the on-screen text; the truth was neither error nor idle, and any delivery of an Enter into that pane would have confirmed a silent model downgrade (the runbook's decline-the-modal rule exists for exactly this; the operator sent one Escape). Traced 2026-08-31: the chain is `StateClassifier.Classify` (internal/robot/activity.go:892) -> `classifyInternal` (:928) -> `classifyState` (:1218-1220, CategoryError takes absolute priority at confidence 0.95) -> `applyHysteresis` (:1279-1290, StateError transitions immediately with no debounce). The one existing guard, `filterErrorToLiveWhenIdle` (:1162), fires only when the live tail shows a fresh idle prompt - by the design note of the closed bd-j5cdo/bd-g6q02/bd-vevxk (stale-scrollback fixes), "the same pattern matching inside the live tail still produces error immediately", so a current on-screen modal is explicitly outside what those fixed. Pattern tables that match quota/exhaustion text: internal/status/errors.go:29-88 and internal/robot/patterns.go:155-167. Consumers acting on a false `error`: internal/coordinator/monitor.go:110-155 (clears SafeToDispatch), internal/robot/health.go:604-605 and :1646-1750 (RestartManager), internal/cli/wait.go:239-242, internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:775.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Let a codex pane hit its provider usage limit until the quota/upgrade modal is on screen with a selection armed (observed on codex CLI, 2026-08-31 00:55Z).
2. `ntm activity <session>` (or the robot state consumers above).
3. Observe state ERROR for a pane that is interactive, waiting on one keystroke, with nothing crashed; `tmux capture-pane -p` shows the modal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The classifier distinguishes a live modal carrying quota/limit/upgrade/confirm text from an error state - either a dedicated state (e.g. needs-operator / modal) or, at minimum, quota-modal patterns excluded from CategoryError with the state falling to a non-error classification; the chosen shape is stated in the code next to the pattern tables.
- [ ] RestartManager and SafeToDispatch treat that classification as not-restartable and not-dispatchable respectively (a modal pane must not receive an automated Enter), verified against the consumer list above.
- [ ] A genuine error string in the live tail still classifies as error with today's confidence and no added debounce.
- [ ] Done when: the reproduction reports the new state, a real crash still reports error, and no consumer in the cited list restarts or dispatches into a modal pane in the integration run.

## Tests

- Unit (Go, classifier): captured modal text fixtures (the codex quota modal verbatim) classify to the new state; existing error fixtures stay error; the stale-scrollback fixtures from bd-j5cdo keep their fixed behavior.
- Integration: a scripted pane painted with the modal text, walked through activity/monitor/health, asserting no restart and no dispatch.

## Blast radius

Confined to the state classification chain in internal/robot/activity.go (classify/hysteresis/filter, ~892-1290), the pattern tables in internal/status/errors.go:29-88 and internal/robot/patterns.go:155-167, and assertions over the cited consumers; their tests. No consumer's own policy logic is rewritten - they react to the new state through their existing switches.
close_reason: live provider modals classified as StateModal/CategoryModal (priority 210-230 over generic error 200), HealthBlocked so restarts never fire into a modal, SafeToDispatch false, scrollback live-window filter; 4 criteria mutation-proven by the implementer; PR 42 merged; scoped go tests green (2 pre-existing env flakes verified present on main); implemented by agy gemini-3.7-flash-high after minimax 402 and bianca session limit

title: Gate pi's permanent chrome on its live spinner, and name pi's own evidence in the verdict
description:
## Outcome

The pi readiness surface answers from pi's own evidence at every layer, and says so. The agent
parser stops reporting a mid-turn `pi` pane as idle; the robot layer stops deciding pi liveness
from wildcard patterns that fire on a braille glyph anywhere in the live window; and both
directions of the verdict carry an indicator that names what was observed on the pane rather
than the token an unrecognised agent reports. Golden captures taken off live panes lock all of
it, so the next reader can tell a working detector from a broken one without running a swarm.

## Steps to Reproduce

The defect this bead was opened for does not reproduce. What follows is the reproduction of
what is actually wrong, which is one layer below the surface that was measured.

1. `p := agent.NewParser()`; load a capture of a `pi` pane mid-turn — one holding pi's spinner
   line (`⠹ Working...`) above its bottom status line.
2. `state, _ := p.ParseWithHint(output, agent.AgentTypePi)`.
3. Observe `state.IsWorking == false` and `state.IsIdle == true` for a pane that is visibly
   working, with `WorkIndicators == ["working..."]`.

`agent.PiActivelyWorking(output, 0)` returns `true` on the same input, so the evidence is
present and unused. The cause is that `detectStateFlags` has no `pi` arm: pi's only idle
pattern is `piPromptChromeRe`, its bottom status line, which is permanent chrome drawn
identically in both states, and `detectIdle` matching it wins over the substring working
heuristics. `internal/status` already gates that chrome on `PiActivelyWorking`
(`unified.go:174-186`), which is why a consumer reading the observer and a consumer reading the
parser got opposite verdicts from the same pane.

A second, narrower reproduction, in the robot layer: call
`robot.IsLiveBusy(screen, "pi", 80)` with a resting pi pane whose transcript quotes another
tool's progress output (`⠙ compiling ntm v1.26.0`). It returns `true`. pi has no entry in
`internal/robot/patterns.go`, so it can only reach `CategoryThinking` through the wildcard
`braille_spinner` pattern, which matches the glyph wherever it lands.

## Context

**The reported defect was verified as not reproducing, on 2026-08-26, against the same binary
the report names (`v1.26.0-93-g4bafe484-dirty`).** Two panes were exercised, both ways, in both
the manual and the `ntm spawn` path:

| pane | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `pi` at rest, 200 columns | `is_idle: true`, `observation_state: idle`, `safe_to_dispatch: true` |
| `pi` at rest, 33 columns (six-pane split) | same |
| `pi` at rest, spawned by `ntm spawn ntm --pi=2 --no-user` | same, both panes |
| `pi` mid-turn, sampled six times | `is_working: true`, `observation_state: working`, `safe_to_dispatch: false` |
| `pi` at rest, screen holding the words "Analyzing… / Processing… / Thinking…" | `is_idle: true`, `safe_to_dispatch: true` |

The fix that closed it is `0a771c3a feat(status): give pi a readiness classifier, and put agy
on the known-type list`, which added the `pi` arm to `determineStateAt`. `git show
4bafe484:internal/status/unified.go` confirms that arm was already in the binary that produced
the readings in the original report, so the report and the code disagree and the code is right.

**Why a working surface read as a broken one, because this is the part worth keeping.** Both
numbers the original report quotes are real and both mislead. `confidence: 0.5` is the agent
parser's bare-header-match floor, not the confidence any consumer gates on — a dispatcher reads
`safe_to_dispatch`, which is fed by the canonical observer's confidence (0.95 on these panes).
And `live_window_thinking` is the `default` arm of `workIndicatorBasis`: it is the token an
agent type with no entry of its own reports, so a correct pi verdict was textually
indistinguishable from a detector that had given up. Naming the evidence is therefore not
cosmetic — it is what makes the difference between the two readable at all, and its absence
cost a P0 investigation.

**What is genuinely broken is one layer in.** The parser defect above means every consumer
reading `agent.Parser` directly gets the opposite verdict from one reading
`status.SessionObserver`. `--robot-is-working` currently lands on the right answer anyway,
because `applyLiveBusyOverride` and `applyCanonicalWorkSafety` both correct it downstream — the
surface is right by compensation rather than by agreement, and the compensating override is
itself firing on a wildcard glyph match rather than on anything pi renders.

**Do not aim at the confidence number**, unchanged from the original report: two independent
hardcoded floors exist (`is_working.go:470-474` pins `0.25` on `StateUnknown`; the parser's
bare-header floor of `0.5` is pinned by `parser_test.go:260-270`), and raising either converts
a wrong answer into a confident wrong answer.

**Not this bead:** `bd-3nv`, the composer classifier that returns `no-classifier` for `pi` and
leaves `ntm spawn` prompt delivery to the operator. Still open, still a different layer.

## Blast radius

Three files and their tests: a short-circuit arm in `internal/agent/parser.go`
(`detectStateFlags`), a type arm in `internal/robot/activity.go` (`IsLiveBusy`), and two switch
cases in `internal/robot/is_working.go` (`workIndicatorBasis`). No pattern in
`internal/agent/patterns.go` changes, no confidence floor moves, and no other agent type's path
is touched. Two new fixtures under `internal/agent/testdata/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ParseWithHint(<mid-turn pi capture>, AgentTypePi)` reports `IsWorking == true` and
      `IsIdle == false`, and the capture used contains pi's idle chrome — so the assertion
      proves the chrome was gated rather than absent
- [ ] `ParseWithHint(<resting pi capture>, AgentTypePi)` reports `IsIdle == true`,
      `IsWorking == false`, `IsInError == false`
- [ ] The indicator sets for the two directions are not equal, asserted directly; a detector
      that answers from the chrome produces the same set for both, so this is the assertion the
      single-direction ones cannot make
- [ ] `IsLiveBusy(screen, "pi", 80)` is `false` for a resting pane whose transcript quotes a
      foreign braille spinner, and `true` for a pane holding pi's own spinner-led `Working` line
- [ ] `workIndicatorBasis` returns `pi_live_spinner` for the working direction and
      `pi_status_line_idle` for the idle one, and the two differ
- [ ] `claude`, `codex` and the wildcard `default` keep the basis tokens they report today,
      asserted in the same table, so the pi arms are additions rather than a reshuffle
- [ ] The `unknown` route is preserved: no confidence floor is raised and no `StateUnknown`
      pane is talked into a verdict
- [ ] Each new test is shown to fail with its own fix reverted, and the failure message names
      the defect
- [ ] Done when: `go test ./internal/agent/ ./internal/robot/ ./internal/status/` is green with
      the pi tests present, and each of them has been observed failing against the unfixed code.

## Tests

- **Unit, table-driven, golden-capture backed** (`internal/agent/parser_test.go`): the verdict
  for each pi capture, both directions, asserting state and indicator set, loaded through the
  existing `loadTestData(t, "<name>.txt")` helper.
- **Unit** (`internal/agent/parser_test.go`): the two directions' indicator sets are unequal.
- **Unit, table-driven** (`internal/robot/is_working_test.go`): `IsLiveBusy` for pi across three
  screens — mid-turn spinner, resting, resting while quoting a foreign spinner.
- **Unit, table-driven** (`internal/robot/is_working_test.go`): `workIndicatorBasis` for pi in
  both directions, plus claude, codex and a wildcard type as unchanged controls.
- **Golden capture:** `internal/agent/testdata/pi_idle.txt` and `pi_working.txt`, taken from
  live panes rather than hand-written, in the form `pi_working_openai.txt` already uses.
close_reason: Landed in PR #12: parser gate, robot routing and named indicators, with golden captures for both directions. The originally reported symptom was verified as not reproducing; the rescoped defect is what shipped.

title: Detect a frozen agent process as its own pane state, distinct from working and idle
description:
## Outcome

A frozen agent process is its own detectable pane state — distinct from working (progressing)
and idle (at prompt): no CPU-time delta AND no screen change across consecutive samples, while
the screen may still show a static "Working..." spinner. Surfaced as its own classification so
tending (and the held-claim actor) can trust it instead of re-deriving it by hand.

## Context

o62l shakedown, 2026-08-31: two pi panes froze mid-model-call (pi has no call timeout — the
documented hang class), one of them holding a claim. Screen-based classification read them as
working/idle; only a hand-run 30 s CPU-delta sample separated frozen from thinking. The tell is
cheap and mechanical; nothing samples it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pane whose process cputime and screen hash are both unchanged across N samples
  classifies as frozen, not working or idle.
- [ ] A pane mid-long-generation (CPU advancing, screen static) never classifies frozen (the
  planted negative — this is exactly the state that must not be killed).
- [ ] The state is visible on the robot surface the tick reads.
- [ ] One mutation per criterion, red recorded.

## Recovery path

Classification only; nothing kills a pane under this bead.

title: activity reports no agents when panes exist but none classify
description:
## Outcome

`ntm activity <session>` distinguishes "this session has no agent panes" from "there are panes
here and none of them could be classified". A session running six agents never reports that it
has none.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a session with live agent processes in its panes — including at least one pane whose
   tmux title is not an NTM-formatted agent name (an agent started outside `ntm spawn`, or one
   whose real process sits more than four levels below the pane's shell).
2. Run `ntm activity <session>`.
3. It prints `No agents found in session` while the panes and their processes are visibly there.

Observed on 2026-08-22 with six live agent processes in the session.

## Context

The message is emitted at `internal/cli/activity.go:591`, inside `renderActivityTUI`, guarded by
`if len(result.Agents) == 0`.

Discovery is **tmux pane inspection**, not a registry and not a process scan.
`collectActivityData` (`internal/cli/activity.go:252-311`) calls `tmux.GetPanes(session)`
(`internal/tmux/session.go:939`), classifies each pane through `detectAgentTypeFromPane`
(`internal/cli/activity.go:314`), and **skips any pane classified `unknown` or `user`**
(`internal/cli/activity.go:267-270`) — before `passesFilter` is ever consulted.

Classification itself is a three-step fallback at `internal/tmux/session.go:3087-3101`:
`parseAgentFromTitle(pane.Title)` looks for an NTM-formatted name such as `cc_1`, then
`pane.Command`, then `detectAgentFromProcessTree`, which walks **four** process levels.

So the empty list means: panes exist, and none of them parsed as a known agent from a title, a
command, or a shallow process walk. That is a **metadata-classification miss reported as an
absence** — the two states are indistinguishable in the output, and the one the operator sees is
the wrong one. An agent launched outside `ntm spawn` keeps its default shell title; an agent
nested more than four levels below the pane's shell defeats the tree walk.

The consequence is not cosmetic: the operator reads "no agents" and starts diagnosing the wrong
thing — whether the session died, whether the spawn worked — while the session is running
normally.

The narrow fix is to stop collapsing the two cases. Anything more — widening the process walk,
adding a fifth detection source — is a separate decision, because a deeper walk costs a `/proc`
traversal per pane on every refresh and this command is a TUI that refreshes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `tmux.GetPanes` returns zero panes, the output says the session has no panes
- [ ] When panes exist but every one classifies as `unknown` or `user`, the output says so and
      reports the count of unclassified panes — it never says "No agents found"
- [ ] The unclassified message names what to check: the pane title, the pane command, and that
      the process may sit deeper than the four levels
      `detectAgentFromProcessTree` walks (`internal/tmux/session.go:3092-3101`)
- [ ] Panes skipped as `user` are counted separately from panes skipped as `unknown` — one is
      expected, the other is a miss
- [ ] `--json` / robot output carries the same distinction as a field, so a caller can tell the
      two states apart without parsing prose
- [ ] The classification logic itself is unchanged: no new detection source and no deeper
      process walk in this bead
- [ ] The command's refresh cost is unchanged — no additional tmux or `/proc` call per pane
- [ ] Done when: a session with panes whose titles are plain shell titles reports "N panes, none
      classified as agents", and a session with no panes at all reports the empty-session
      message.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven in the convention of `internal/cli/activity_test.go` (plain
`func Test…` with case slices, e.g. `TestPassesFilter` at `:72`), over a stubbed pane list so no
tmux server is needed:

- zero panes → empty-session message
- panes present, all `unknown` → unclassified message with the correct count
- panes present, all `user` → its own message, counted separately
- a mix of `user`, `unknown` and one classified agent → the agent is rendered and the skipped
  counts are reported
- one classified agent only → today's output, unchanged (regression)
- the `--json` shape for each of the above → the state is a field, asserted by round-trip

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is a branch and a message.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/activity.go` — the skip at `267-270`, the empty guard and message at `591`, and
the result struct that carries the counts to the JSON path. `internal/tmux/session.go` is
**read, not modified**: `GetPanes` (`:939`) and the classification fallback (`3087-3101`) keep
their current behaviour, which is what makes this bead small and its regression risk local to
one command.

title: Deliver the recovery_context step to pi panes: readiness times out at state=unknown 0.25
description:
## Outcome

`ntm spawn` delivers the **recovery_context** step to `pi` panes, so a mixed
`pi` + `cc` swarm launches with every pane prompted instead of every `pi` pane failing
`recovery_context readiness ... timeout ... last state=unknown freshness=fresh confidence=0.25`
while sitting at a healthy pi prompt. The contradiction the same run prints — a
`no-classifier` verdict that tells the operator delivery was "allowed unchecked", next to a
30s readiness gate that in fact blocked delivery for that very pane — is resolved: either the
gate stops applying to a type the verdict declares unchecked, or the verdict stops claiming it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Installed binary `v1.26.0-93-g4bafe484-dirty` (`/home/gabriel/.local/bin/ntm`, rebuilt
   2026-08-25 23:35). It already carries the whole `bd-ffv3d` line of fixes: `9e16209c`
   ("detect pi panes in detectAgentTypeFromPane"), `fa4a869f` ("detect a pi pane by its
   command, because pi destroys its own title") and the tests around them.
2. From `~/repositories/agent-usage-book`:

   ```
   ntm spawn agent-usage-book \
     --pi 2:deepseek-v4-pro-high-k1 --pi 2:deepseek-v4-pro-high-k2 \
     --pi 2:deepseek-v4-pro-high-k3 --cc 1:sonnet \
     --stagger-mode=fixed --stagger-delay=15s --no-cass-context --prompt '<swarm marching orders>'
   ```
3. Seven panes come up; all six pi panes reach a working pi prompt.
4. All six pi panes fail, the single `cc` pane succeeds:

   ```
   ⚠ Warning: spawn prompt delivery failed for agent 1: recovery_context readiness for pane %66:
   timeout waiting for pane %66 to become ready; last state=unknown freshness=fresh confidence=0.25
   ⚠ pane %66 (pi): no-classifier — no composer classifier for this agent type; send the prompt by hand
   ✓ pane %72 (cc): checked-and-ready
   Error: spawn prompt setup failed: pane %66: agent 1 (pi): recovery_context readiness ... (×6)
   ```

   Recovery is manual delivery to six panes.

Observed 2026-08-25, one run, 6 of 6 pi panes. Two things differ from `bd-ffv3d`, which is the
reason this is a separate bead rather than a comment on that one:

- the failing step is **`recovery_context`**, not `user_prompt`. `bd-ffv3d`'s three
  reproductions (2026-08-22 15:20, 2026-08-23 17:57, 2026-08-23 21:20) all name `user_prompt`.
- the run passed `--no-cass-context`, and a recovery context was prepared and dispatched
  anyway (`✓ Recovery context prepared for session`), so the step that fails is one nobody
  asked for on a freshly created session with no panes to recover.

## Context

**`bd-ffv3d` is IN_REVIEW and its fixes are installed, so this is not that bead reopened.**
That bead traced the failure to pane-type resolution and fixed it in two places
(`detectAgentTypeFromPane`, plus command-based detection because pi rewrites its own title).
Whatever remains here survives those fixes and shows up one step earlier in the sequence.

**Where the failure sits.** `dispatchSpawnPromptSequence` (`internal/cli/spawn.go`) walks the
step list and gates each step on readiness, wrapping the failure with the step kind:
`internal/cli/spawn.go:4073` builds `"%s readiness for pane %s: %w"`. The recovery step is
appended at `internal/cli/spawn.go:3997` as `spawnPromptStep{Kind: "recovery_context"}`. The
timeout body comes from `spawnReadinessError` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:6081`) off the same poll
`bd-ffv3d` documents: `StateUnknown` is pinned to confidence 0.25 by `observationConfidence`
(`internal/status/unified.go`) and `SafeToDispatch` demands 0.75, so an unknown state can never
pass, however fresh the capture is.

**The contradiction worth starting from.** `spawnPaneReadinessVerdict`
(`internal/cli/spawn.go:4027`) computes its verdict **from the requested agent type alone** —
`ComposerClassifierVerdict` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2426`) returns `no-classifier` whenever
`composerMarkerForAgent` has no entry, and `pi` has none. Its own comment says the
`no-classifier` line names manual delivery "because delivery was allowed unchecked". But
delivery was **not** allowed unchecked: the readiness poll ran, timed out after 30s and failed
the pane. So one run prints two mutually exclusive statements about the same pane. Deciding
which one is true is the first question this bead has to answer — it determines whether the fix
is "skip the readiness gate for a type with no classifier" or "give pi a composer classifier
and make the verdict mean something".

**Second angle, cheap to check:** why a recovery context exists at all for a brand-new session
spawned with `--no-cass-context`. If the recovery step is skippable when there is nothing to
recover, the six panes would have proceeded to `user_prompt` — which is `bd-ffv3d`'s territory,
not a fix, but it isolates which of the two gates still bites.

**Do not re-derive from the `bd-zz717` angle.** Per-pane verdicts are already printed; this
bead is delivery still failing with the verdict visible, not nobody being told.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `pi` pane at a healthy prompt passes the readiness gate for the `recovery_context`
      step, or that step is not gated for `pi` — decided explicitly and the reason recorded in
      the code, not left to whichever branch was easier.
- [ ] The `no-classifier` verdict line and the actual dispatch behaviour agree for every agent
      type: a type reported as `no-classifier` is not silently blocked by a 30s readiness poll,
      and a type that is gated is not reported as "allowed unchecked".
- [ ] Re-running the exact command in *Steps to Reproduce* delivers the prompt to 6 of 6 pi
      panes plus the `cc` pane, with no `spawn prompt setup failed` and no manual send.
- [ ] Whether `--no-cass-context` should also suppress the recovery_context step for a
      newly created session is answered in the bead's closing comment — fixed or explicitly
      declined, not left unstated.
- [ ] Done when: a 6-pane `pi` + 1-pane `cc` spawn on the installed binary reports every pane
      delivered, and the failing case is covered by a test that fails without the fix.

## Tests

- **Unit** over `dispatchSpawnPromptSequence`: a `pi` pane, a step list whose first step is
  `recovery_context`, and an observation that classifies the pane as ready — currently no test
  exercises a non-`cc`/`cod` type succeeding through this gate for that step kind.
  `TestDispatchSpawnPromptSequenceReadinessTimeout` covers `AgentClaude` timing out only.
- **Unit** over the verdict/gate agreement: for each agent type, assert that
  `spawnPaneReadinessVerdict` returning `no-classifier` implies the dispatch path does not
  block on readiness (or the inverse invariant, whichever the fix chooses). Break it on purpose
  before trusting it — a table test over types passes trivially if the invariant is written to
  match today's behaviour.
- **E2E**, the reproduction above, run against the built binary; it is the only level that
  catches a pane whose type resolves differently in a real tmux session than in a fixture.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/spawn.go` (the step loop, the verdict helper, the recovery-step append) and
possibly `internal/tmux/session.go`'s composer-marker table if the chosen fix is to give `pi` a
classifier. No schema, no persisted state, no change to the `spawn` command surface.

title: Empty the tmux socket guard's legacy list
description:
## Outcome

`tmuxSocketGuardLegacy` is empty and deleted, because every tmux invocation in test code
addresses an explicit socket. The ratchet stops being a list of exemptions and becomes a plain
rule.

## Context

`bd-wkq` made the tmux clients that own a private server address it with `-S`, and added a
repo-wide guard (`tests/tmux_socket_guard_test.go`) that fails on a new unsocketed
`kill-server` / `kill-session` / `new-session`. It could not fix the calls that already existed
without growing far past its own blast radius, so it snapshotted them: **41 files, 121 tolerated
calls**, each file permitted the count it had on 2026-08-28 and no more.

Those calls are not unguarded today. Each lives in a package whose `TestMain` calls
`testutil.IsolateTmuxTestProcess`, which sets `TMUX_TMPDIR` for the whole test binary and
hard-exits rather than falling back. That is a real net, and it is not the one that failed — but
it is a coarser one, keyed on a process-wide environment variable rather than on the argv of the
command that does the killing, and `bd-9oo` already recorded one way that variable stops being
true.

The concentration matters for planning: six files hold 59 of the 121.

```
 24  tests/integration/tui_parity_handlers_test.go
 13  tests/e2e/robot_mode_test.go
  7  tests/e2e/multi_session_test.go
  5  e2e/spawn_assignment_cli_e2e_test.go
  5  tests/e2e/agent_registration_test.go
  5  tests/e2e/crash_recovery_test.go
```

**Why this is worth doing rather than leaving the ratchet forever.** A tolerated list that never
shrinks reads, after a few months, as a list of things that are fine. The guard's own stale-entry
check fires when a file drops below its count, which makes shrinking the list mechanical: fix a
file, the guard tells you to lower its number, lower it, and the exemption is gone. That loop
only runs if somebody starts it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every entry removed from `tmuxSocketGuardLegacy`, and the map itself deleted along with the
      code that reads it, so the guard has one rule and no exemptions
- [ ] Each converted call addresses its socket explicitly, through `-L`/`-S` or through a client
      built by `tmux.NewClientWithSocket`, matching what `bd-wkq` established
- [ ] No package loses coverage: the tests that were converted still run and still assert what
      they asserted, verified by running each touched package
- [ ] The full suite is run in the container with a decoy (`NTM_TEST_DECOY=1
      scripts/test-in-container.sh`) and the decoy survives — the same check `bd-wkq` closed on
- [ ] Done when: `tmuxSocketGuardLegacy` no longer exists and the guard is green

## Tests

- Unit, the existing guard: it is the acceptance check for this bead, and it passes only when the
  list is empty because a stale entry fails it too.
- Integration, per-package runs of every package touched, in the container, to prove the conversions did not
  change what the tests exercise.
- Integration, the container decoy run described above.

## Blast radius

The 41 files named in `tmuxSocketGuardLegacy` plus the guard itself. Concentrated enough to be
split: the six files above are half the work and can land separately from the tail of 35 files
holding one or two calls each. No production code is touched — `bd-wkq` already added everything
`internal/tmux` needs.

## Recovery path

Test-only. Reverting restores the tolerated list and today's behaviour; nothing is migrated.

title: Record per-pane attribution on assignment claims and expose each pane's CLI session id
description:
## Outcome

A bead claimed by `ntm assign` carries attribution that is true of the pane it was claimed for:
`agent_name`, `harness` and `model` come from the assignment item rather than from the `ntm`
process environment, and each pane's agent CLI session identifier is reachable from a robot surface
so that a bead can be joined to the transcript that recorded its token spend.

## Context

The wiring for this already exists and is fed from the wrong place, which is why it produces
nothing rather than producing something wrong.

`insertGuardedClaimEvent` (`internal/bv/bv.go:2051-2074`) writes every guarded claim and release
into the beads `events` table with `agent_name`, `harness` and `model` columns already in the
INSERT. Their values come from `nullableEnvironment("BR_AGENT_NAME")`, `("BR_HARNESS")` and
`("BR_MODEL")`, read with `os.Getenv` inside the `ntm` process, and nothing in `ntm` ever sets
them. Measured on 2026-08-25 across two real trackers: 0 of 1,011 events in `llm-workflow` and
0 of 1,525 in `agent-usage-book` carry any of the three.

**Exporting them would not fix it, and that is the point.** One `ntm` process claims for many panes
of different agent types and different models in the same run, so a process-level variable cannot
vary per pane. The three columns are process-global by construction, which is why they are empty
rather than wrong: there is no correct value to export.

The values are already in hand at the exact call site. `internal/cli/assign.go:3014-3017` composes
the actor from `item.AgentName`, falling back to `session-agentType-pane-W-P`, and that actor flows
into `atomicCoordinator.Execute(..., Actor: actor, ...)` at `:3040` and reaches
`bv.ClaimBeadForAssignmentWithOperatorGatedLabels` at `:3113`. The agent type is right there. One
gap is honest and belongs in the work: it was not confirmed that the assign-time `AssignmentItem`
carries a resolved model the way the spawn-time `spawnedAgentInfo` struct does
(`internal/cli/spawn.go:4352-4360`), so the model may have to be threaded from spawn to assign
rather than read where the other two are read.

The claim path deliberately does not go through `br`. `ClaimBeadForAssignment` is documented as
"intentionally limited to assignment paths and never delegates to br's generic `--claim` behavior"
(`internal/bv/bv.go:1286-1289`), and `claimBeadForAssignmentTransaction`
(`internal/bv/bv.go:1593-1706`) opens the SQLite file and does its own compare-and-set. So this is
not fixable from outside `ntm` by any caller: `bin/swarm-dispatch` in the `llm-workflow` repo runs
`ntm assign "$session" --auto --strategy=dependency --template=custom --template-file "$f"
--reserve-files=false --json` and never claims anything itself, and the swarm's own operating skill
forbids a pane from pre-claiming, because a pre-claimed bead is refused as held by another actor.

**The second half is a join nobody has.** A consumer that wants to attribute token spend to a bead
needs `bead -> pane -> the transcript file that pane's CLI wrote`. The first edge exists in the
`actor` column. The last edge exists in each CLI's own session directory. The middle edge exists
nowhere: `ntm` knows which agent CLI it started in which pane, and does not expose that CLI's
session identifier anywhere a reader can reach. Without it, attribution is inference over
timestamps rather than a join, and the consumer that needs it is a measurement tool whose stated
rule is that a number it cannot justify is not printed.

Related, and separate: `AGENT_NAME` with no prefix is already read as an ambient fallback by the
mail and lock paths (`internal/cli/mail.go:775-779`, `:789-809`), so the pattern of reading an
identity from the environment already exists here. It is simply not wired to attribution, and the
fix is the opposite direction anyway, from the item rather than from the environment.

The actor string's own format is not decided here. It is a convention several producers must share,
including ones outside this repo, and it is owned by `lw-hvlk` in the `llm-workflow` tracker. This
bead should conform to whatever that settles rather than inventing a fourth shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agent_name`, `harness` and `model` on a claim event come from the assignment item, so that
      two panes of different agent types claimed in one `ntm assign` run record different values
- [ ] The process environment stays as the fallback for claim paths that have no assignment item,
      so no existing caller loses behaviour it has today
- [ ] Where the assign-time item has no resolved model, the bead states whether the model was
      threaded from the spawn path or left empty, rather than recording a guess
- [ ] The agent CLI session identifier for each pane is exposed on an existing robot surface, named
      alongside the pane's agent type, so `bead -> pane -> transcript` is a join rather than a
      timestamp correlation
- [ ] A claim made in a session with two panes of different agent types produces two events whose
      `agent_name` and `harness` differ, verified by reading the events table after the run
- [ ] An empty or missing value is recorded as NULL rather than as an empty string, so a consumer
      can tell "not known" from "known to be blank"
- [ ] Done when: reading the events table of a tracker a real two-pane swarm has claimed against
      shows attribution that differs per pane, and the transcript of each pane is reachable from
      what the robot surface reports

## Tests

- **Unit (Go):** the attribution values passed to `insertGuardedClaimEvent` are taken from the item
  when present and from the environment when the item carries none, asserted for each of the three
  fields independently. A test that only checks the item path would pass while the fallback is
  broken
- **Unit (Go):** an item with an empty model records NULL rather than an empty string
- **Integration:** an assignment run against a temporary tracker with two items of different agent
  types produces two claim events whose `agent_name` and `harness` differ. This is the test that
  fails today, and it is the one that proves the process-global defect is gone
- **Integration:** the robot surface reports a session identifier for each pane, and the value
  matches a file that exists in that CLI's session directory. A field that is present and points at
  nothing is worse than an absent field, because a consumer will join on it

## Blast radius

`internal/bv/bv.go` around the guarded-claim insert, `internal/cli/assign.go` around the item that
already composes the actor, and whichever robot output struct carries per-pane state. No change to
the claim transaction's own compare-and-set semantics, to the actor string's format, or to any
caller outside this repo: `bin/swarm-dispatch` keeps the same command line.

## Recovery path

The change is additive to columns that are already written and currently NULL, so nothing existing
is rewritten and no historical event changes. Backing it out returns the three fields to the
process environment they read today, which is empty, and returns the tracker to exactly its current
state.

comments.text:
Model-field decision (bd-4gw)

Checked whether the assign-time AssignmentItem carries a resolved model the way spawn-time
spawnedAgentInfo does. It does not, and there is no reliable path to get one without new
cross-process persistence:

- AssignmentItem (internal/cli/assign.go) has no Model field at all.
- The only model-shaped data available at assign time is assignAgentInfo.model, populated by
  detectModelFromTitle (internal/cli/assign.go): a substring match against "opus"/"sonnet"/"haiku"
  in the pane's tmux title. It only recognizes Claude Code model names, returns "" for every other
  agent type, and is never even copied onto AssignmentItem today — it is a guess, not resolved data,
  and the bead explicitly rules out recording a guess.
- spawn-time's spawnedAgentInfo.resolvedModel (internal/cli/spawn.go) is computed from
  persona/config/plugin-map at spawn, but nothing persists it anywhere the assign path can read
  later. The one per-pane file that does bridge spawn to assign — the Agent Mail pane identity file
  (internal/agentmail/pane_identity.go, written by registerSpawnedAgents) — carries only the agent
  name string, not the model.

Threading a real resolved model into assign would require extending that identity-file mechanism
to also carry the model, which touches internal/agentmail and internal/cli/spawn.go — outside this
bead's stated blast radius (internal/bv/bv.go, internal/cli/assign.go, the robot per-pane output
struct).

Decision: leave `model` NULL on the assignment-claim attribution path. ClaimAttribution.Model
(internal/assignment/atomic.go) is defined and threaded end-to-end (falls back to BR_MODEL when
set, records SQL NULL when neither is present — never an empty string), but nothing on the assign
path populates it yet. This is the bead's own permitted "leave it empty" branch, not a workaround.
Threading it for real is follow-on work once the identity-file (or an equivalent per-pane store) is
extended to carry a resolved model.

title: Surface a stale or failing bv instead of answering with nothing
description:
## Outcome

When the external `bv` binary is too old for the capabilities ntm asks of it, or fails outright,
`ntm work history` and `ntm work burndown` say so on stdout. Neither command can present a
degraded or empty answer as a real one, and the test suite can no longer pass while every real
`bv` failure mode goes unhandled.

## Steps to Reproduce

**A — `work history` reports zeros as data.** With `bv` v0.16.1 installed and a tracker whose
commit subjects all carry their bead ids, run `ntm work history`. It reports
`beads_with_commits: 0` over ~107 beads, every bead with `"commits":[]` and `"commit_index":{}`.
Nothing warns that the number is not a measurement.

**B — `work burndown` prints nothing.** Run `ntm work burndown current`. stdout receives zero
bytes. `bv --robot-burndown current` exits 1 and writes the plain text `No active sprint found`
to **stderr**, not JSON.

Both observed on 2026-08-22.

## Context

**Neither number is computed in this repo, and that is the key fact.**

`runWorkHistory` (`internal/cli/work.go:2734`) calls
`tools.NewBVAdapter().GetHistory` → `runRobotCommand(ctx, dir, "--robot-history")`
(`internal/tools/bv.go:226`, `:314`), which shells out to `bv` and passes its raw JSON through
unchanged in `--json` mode. ntm's own `HistoryStats` (`internal/cli/work.go:2663-2667`) carries
only `total_beads`, `total_commits` and `correlated_count` — **`beads_with_commits` is not an ntm
field at all**; it comes from `bv`, and the commit-subject matching that produces it lives inside
that binary.

`runWorkBurndown` (`internal/cli/work.go:3061`, command at `:2633` with `cobra.ExactArgs(1)`)
calls `adapter.GetBurndown` → `--robot-burndown <sprint>` (`internal/tools/bv.go:230`).
`runRobotCommand` (`internal/tools/bv.go:349-353`) turns any non-zero exit into a Go error, which
`runWorkBurndown` returns immediately — before any parsing or rendering. `cli.Execute()`
(`internal/cli/root.go:3155`, error path around `:3181-3202`) prints it as
`Error: …` on **stderr**. So there is no missing writer and no early return in ntm's render
path: `renderBurndown` (`internal/cli/work.go:3090`) always prints when it is reached, and it is
simply never reached. "Prints nothing" is what a stdout-only reader sees.

**The capability gate is the thing to distrust here, and it is wrong in the direction nobody
checked.** `internal/tools/bv.go:87-92` gates `robot_history` and `robot_burndown` behind
`bv >= 0.31`, and `robot_triage` / `robot_plan` / `robot_insights` / `robot_next` behind
`>= 0.30`. **No such `bv` has ever been published.** The tap that serves this machine reports
`dicklesworthstone/tap/bv: 0.16.1 -> stable 0.16.2` (read 2026-08-23), so every version the table
names is above everything that exists.

And the gated modes answer anyway on 0.16.1: `--robot-history` returned well-formed JSON, and
`--robot-burndown current` exited 1 with `No active sprint found` — a sprint lookup that ran, not
an unimplemented mode refusing. So the table reports as absent a capability the binary serves.

That inverts the obvious fix. A warning driven off the version comparison would fire on **every
run, for every user, forever**, and would call a working capability missing. The numbers in that
table are the first defect; the silence on real failure is the second. This bead fixes both, and
the reporting must key off observed behaviour rather than off the comparison.

**Why this shipped, and this is the part worth fixing hardest.** The contract test
(`internal/tools/contract_test.go:820-862`, table-driven `modeTest{name,key,call}`) runs against
a **fake `bv`** shell script at `testdata/faketools/bv`, injected by overriding `PATH`
(`internal/cli/work_test.go:195`). The fake always returns well-formed, non-empty JSON. It never
emulates a real `bv` that returns zero counts, that writes a plain-text error to stderr and
exits 1, or that reports a version below the capability gate. So the suite proves that a JSON
shape round-trips and nothing about how real `bv` behaviour is handled — a green test suite over
three live defects.

**The upstream half is explicitly out of scope.** `beads_with_commits` being zero while commit
subjects carry bead ids is a defect *inside* `bv`, in a repo this bead does not touch. The rule
here is the same one applied to `br`: a third-party tool gets an upstream issue or nothing.
What is in scope is that ntm must not present that number as though it measured it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The capability requirements at `internal/tools/bv.go:87-92` are corrected to versions that
      exist and that reflect what `bv` actually serves, verified by exercising each gated robot
      mode against the installed binary rather than by trusting the current numbers
- [ ] Degradation is reported from observed behaviour, never from the version comparison alone: a
      warning fires when a robot mode is unavailable or errors, and a `bv` that answers produces
      no warning at all
- [ ] When a warning does fire, `ntm work history` and `ntm work burndown` print it on **stdout**
      with the answer, naming the installed version and the capability that failed
- [ ] A non-zero exit from `bv` is surfaced on stdout, with `bv`'s own stderr text included, not
      only through the generic `Error:` path at `internal/cli/root.go:3181-3202`
- [ ] `ntm work burndown` with no active sprint prints a message a reader can act on and exits
      non-zero — zero bytes on stdout is never the answer
- [ ] `--json` output for both commands carries the degradation as a field (the `bv` version, the
      required version, whether the answer is complete), so an orchestrator can tell a real zero
      from an unavailable one
- [ ] `beads_with_commits` and its neighbours are passed through with their source named, so no
      reader takes an ntm-branded number for an ntm-computed one
- [ ] The fake `bv` at `testdata/faketools/bv` gains the real failure modes: a non-zero exit with
      plain-text stderr, a version below the gate, and a well-formed response with zero counts
- [ ] Each of those three fake behaviours is asserted by a test that **fails against today's
      code** — demonstrated by running it before the fix, not assumed
- [ ] A `bv` that serves every capability a command needs prints no warning — asserted, so the
      fix cannot degrade into an unconditional banner
- [ ] The existing contract cases keep passing unchanged
- [ ] Done when: with `bv` 0.16.1 installed, `ntm work history` prints its numbers with no
      spurious version warning, `ntm work burndown current` prints why it has nothing to show,
      and the only thing that warns is a capability the binary genuinely does not serve.

## Tests

**Unit tests** in the existing table-driven convention of
`internal/tools/contract_test.go:820-862`, driven by an extended fake `bv` under
`testdata/faketools/` selected by `PATH` (`internal/cli/work_test.go:195`):

- fake `bv` exits 1 with plain-text stderr → the text reaches stdout and the exit is non-zero
- fake `bv` reports a version below the gate but answers the robot mode → no warning (the case
  today's table gets wrong, and the one that would become a permanent banner)
- fake `bv` reports a version below the gate and refuses the robot mode → warning naming the
  installed version and the mode, and the command still answers what it can
- fake `bv` reports a version above the gate → no warning, output unchanged (regression)
- fake `bv` returns well-formed JSON with zero counts → the numbers are rendered with their
  source named
- fake `bv` returns malformed JSON → a message naming the tool, not a parse panic
- `work burndown` with no sprint argument → cobra's `ExactArgs(1)` message, unchanged

Plus one **end-to-end** case per command against the fake, asserting stdout is non-empty in every
failure mode — the single property that was missing.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is a subprocess boundary and its
messages.

## Recovery path

Nothing here migrates or writes state — both commands are read-only over `bv` and the tracker.
If the added warning proves too noisy, it is one revert of `internal/cli/work.go` and
`internal/tools/bv.go`; the capability table at `internal/tools/bv.go:88-107` is not being
changed, so no behaviour depends on the new code staying in place.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/work.go` (`runWorkHistory` at `2734`, `runWorkBurndown` at `3061`, `renderBurndown`
at `3090`), `internal/tools/bv.go` (`runRobotCommand` at `349-353` and the capability gate it
already carries at `88-107`), and the fake tool under `testdata/faketools/bv` plus the contract
tests. **No change to `bv` itself** — the zero-count defect is upstream and stays there; this
bead only stops ntm from repeating it silently.

title: Classify every robot query for session scope, and refuse an ignored --session
description:
## Outcome

Every registered `--robot-*` flag is classified in code as honouring `--session` or refusing it,
and a query in the refusing column that is handed `--session` returns `success:false` with a
machine-readable code and a hint, instead of accepting the flag and answering about a scope the
caller did not ask for. A robot query added later that is in neither column turns the test suite
red.

## Context

Split out of `bd-jlv68`, which scopes `--robot-snapshot` and settles the spelling: **the scope is
`--session`**, the shared root flag at `internal/cli/root.go:4787`, resolved through the
`resolveRobot…Session` helpers at `:5387-5401`. This bead is the sweep that applies that decision
to the whole surface.

**The inventory, measured 2026-08-23.** There are **154** registered `--robot-*` flags, declared
from `internal/cli/root.go:4118` through `:4691`. They are dispatched by the `Run:` closure of
`rootCmd` at `internal/cli/root.go:733-3144` — *not* by the if-chain at `:6346`, which is
`needsConfigLoading`, a config gate. They divide like this:

| bucket | count | what it is | column |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 4 | already resolve `--session` — `--robot-pipeline-run`, `--robot-tokens`, `--robot-alerts`, `--robot-palette` | honours |
| B | 50 | take the session as their own flag's value, e.g. `--robot-tail=proj` | refuses |
| C | 8 | per-session payload, ignore `--session` today | honours, after their own beads |
| D | 86 | no session dimension: tracker, config, doctor, accounts, quota, integrations | refuses |
| E | 6 | fleet aggregates | split by their own beads |

**The silent failure is measured, not hypothesised.** `--session` is registered on the same
`cobra.Command.Flags()` set as every robot flag, and cobra performs no cross-flag validation, so
it parses cleanly beside all 153 others and is then read in four dispatch branches only. Two
proofs from the code: `--robot-status` (`:763-772`) calls `robot.PrintStatusWithOptions`, whose
signature has no session argument, so `ntm --robot-status --session=foo` returns fleet-wide
status; and `ntm --robot-tail=proj1 --session=proj2` (`:1631-1650`) reads `robotTail` and never
references `robotSharedSession`, so `proj2` is accepted and discarded without a word.

**Why bucket B refuses rather than converges.** Those 50 flags already carry their session as
their own value, and rewriting them into booleans plus `--session` would change half the robot
API's call syntax — every script, skill reference and doc that spells `--robot-tail=<session>`.
The repo owes no backwards compatibility (`AGENTS.md`, *Backwards Compatibility*), so that
rewrite is permitted, but it is a different and much larger piece of work than this sweep. Here,
`--session` alongside a bucket-B flag is refused, because a value that is accepted and discarded
is the exact defect this bead exists to end.

**Bucket C and E are settled elsewhere, and this bead depends on all of them**, because the
classification table can only be frozen once nothing is still moving between columns: the seven
bespoke session flags converge onto `--session` in their own bead, `--robot-rano-stats` gains a
filter in its own, `--robot-status` / `--robot-dashboard` / `--robot-terse` gain a scope in one
more, `--robot-snapshot` is `bd-jlv68`, and `--robot-inspect-coordination` /`--robot-restore` are
a `question` bead. This bead lands last and freezes the result.

**The error vocabulary does get one addition, and the earlier claim that it does not was wrong.**
None of the existing codes says what a refusal here means: `INVALID_FLAG`
(`internal/robot/types.go:92`) says the flag does not exist, but `--session` does exist and the
caller spelled it correctly — and reusing it makes `suggestNearestFlag`
(`internal/cli/root.go:456-486`) offer a "did you mean" for a flag that was typed right.
`SESSION_NOT_FOUND` (`:86`) says the session is missing, which is a different fact.
`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is exit code 2, documented in `AGENTS.md` as "skip gracefully" — the opposite
of what a caller should do here. So the refusal gets its own code.

Verified before this bead was written: **no wrapper in this repository passes `--session`
unconditionally to robot queries**, so turning acceptance into an error breaks no existing
caller. The single non-Go hit is `scripts/integration_master_test.sh:353`, which passes
`--session` to the `ntm history` subcommand, not to a robot flag.

Precedent for this class of defect in the same area: ntm#214, a deprecation hint pointing at a
flag that did not exist; its regression test is `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every one of the 154 registered `--robot-*` flags appears in exactly one column of a single
      classification table in code — honours `--session`, or refuses it — with no flag listed
      twice and none missing
- [ ] Passing `--session` to a flag in the refusing column returns `success:false`, exit code 1,
      and a new machine-readable `error_code` distinct from `INVALID_FLAG`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`
      and `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`
- [ ] That refusal carries a hint saying either which flag scopes this query (for the 50 that
      carry their session as their own value) or that the query has no session dimension (for the
      86 that do not)
- [ ] The new code is added to `internal/robot/types.go:86-92` alongside the existing constants
      and is documented in the error-code table in `AGENTS.md`
- [ ] `--robot-session` keeps returning `INVALID_FLAG` with the near-miss hint from
      `suggestNearestFlag` (`internal/cli/root.go:456-486`), and that hint names `--session`
- [ ] A test enumerates the registered `robot-*` flags from `rootCmd` at runtime and fails when a
      flag is in neither column — so a query added later cannot skip the decision
- [ ] Every query in the honouring column actually filters: for each, the scoped answer differs
      from the unscoped one when more than one session is live
- [ ] No robot query changes its output for a call that passes no `--session`
- [ ] The refusal path serialises a complete `RobotResponse` (`internal/robot/types.go:227-260`)
      with `success:false`, a non-empty `error_code` and no partial payload beside it
- [ ] Done when: `ntm --robot-tail=proj1 --session=proj2` is refused instead of silently
      answering about `proj1`, and adding a robot flag without classifying it turns the suite red.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, in the style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go` (cobra
`ParseFlags` against a throwaway command), driven from the classification table so the whole list
is covered rather than a sample:

- `--session` on each refusing-column flag → refusal with the new code and a hint
- `--session` on each honouring-column flag → accepted, and the scoped answer differs from the
  unscoped one
- `--robot-tail=proj1 --session=proj2` → refused, naming that `--robot-tail` carries its own
  session
- no `--session` passed → output unchanged from today, per query family (regression)
- `--robot-session` → `INVALID_FLAG` plus the near-miss hint naming `--session`
- the four bucket-A queries' resolution precedence → unchanged

**Unit test over the flag registry**: enumerate `rootCmd`'s `robot-…` flags at runtime, assert
each is in the table, and assert the table names no flag that is not registered — the case that
fails both when a query is added unclassified and when one is removed.

**Envelope round-trip test**, in the style of `internal/robot/envelope_test.go` and
`internal/robot/tui_parity_test.go:1177`: each refusal marshals and unmarshals to a complete
`RobotResponse`.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is flag parsing and JSON shape.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the robot flag declarations (`:4118-4691`), the dispatch closure
(`:733-3144`) where the refusal is applied in front of the handlers, the shared resolution
helpers (`:5387-5401`, `:4787`) and the error classification path (`:417-486`) — plus one new
classification table with its test, one new constant in `internal/robot/types.go:86-92`, and the
error-code table in `AGENTS.md`. **No robot query's payload computation is touched**: this bead
adds a guard in front of queries that ignore a flag and wires the ones that already scope into
the same table. Anything that gains a new filter is one of the beads this one depends on.

Both are the accepted-and-ignored failure this bead ends. Note the exit-code convention the refusal must follow: a robot failure is carried in the JSON body and turned into a non-zero exit by encodeTerminalRobotOutput (internal/robot/robot.go:7742-7754) reaching recordRobotProcessExit (internal/cli/root.go:845-847); a nil Go error with success:false in the body is not enough on every handler, and --robot-status is one that exits 0 today.

title: Scope the fleet aggregates --robot-status, --robot-dashboard and --robot-terse to one session
description:
## Outcome

`--robot-status`, `--robot-dashboard` and `--robot-terse` accept `--session` and answer about
that session alone, resolving it the same way `--robot-snapshot` does. Unscoped, each behaves
exactly as it does today. The four fleet aggregates stop being the only state surfaces an
orchestrator cannot narrow.

## Context

These three are fleet aggregates: they walk every session and every pane and answer about all of
them, with no filter of any kind.

- `--robot-status` (`internal/cli/root.go:763-772`) calls
  `robot.PrintStatusWithOptions(pagination)` — the call takes no session argument at all
- `--robot-dashboard` (`:1013-1014`) calls `robot.PrintDashboard(jsonOutput)`
- `--robot-terse` (`:2544-2545`) calls `robot.PrintTerse(cfg)`

`--session` is registered on the same flag set (`internal/cli/root.go:4787`) as every other robot
flag, so cobra parses it here without complaint and the value is then never read. Measured
2026-08-23: `ntm --robot-status --session=foo` returns fleet-wide status, silently. That is the
defect this bead removes for three of the four aggregates; the fourth, `--robot-snapshot`, is
`bd-jlv68`, which establishes the convention this bead follows rather than reinventing.

They are one bead because they are one shape: three read-only aggregations over the same session
and pane inventory, differing in rendering. Splitting them would triple the cost of a change that
is a filter applied at the same place three times.

The resolution path to reuse is the one the four bucket-A queries already use —
`resolveRobot…Session` (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`) falling back to `robotSharedSession`
(`:4787`), with precedence covered by `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49`.

The remaining two ambiguous flags are **not** in this bead. `--robot-inspect-coordination`
(`:2679`) is keyed by agent name, and NATO-phonetic agent names repeat across sessions;
`--robot-restore` (`:2598`) is keyed by a save-file path that may itself name a session. Both are
decisions rather than filters, and they carry their own `question` bead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of `--robot-status`, `--robot-dashboard` and `--robot-terse` accepts `--session` and
      returns only that session's sessions/panes/agents data
- [ ] Each resolves the session through the shared helper path (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`),
      not through three separate resolutions written per query
- [ ] Called with no `--session`, each produces output byte-identical to today's — asserted, not
      assumed
- [ ] A `--session` naming a session that does not exist returns `success:false` with
      `error_code: SESSION_NOT_FOUND` for all three, never an empty success
- [ ] The scoped answer of each differs from its unscoped answer whenever more than one session
      is live — the criterion that proves the filter is applied rather than accepted
- [ ] Pagination on `--robot-status` (`robot.PrintStatusWithOptions`) keeps working under a
      scope: limits and offsets apply to the filtered set, not to the fleet
- [ ] The four bucket-A queries and `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go:1-49` are untouched
- [ ] Done when: with two live sessions, `ntm --robot-status --session <one>` names only that
      session's panes, and `ntm --robot-status` still names both.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, over a stubbed session and pane inventory so no tmux server is
needed, in the style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go`:

- each query scoped to one of two stub sessions → only that session's entries
- each query unscoped → both sessions, output unchanged from today (regression)
- unknown session name → `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` for each
- `--robot-status` scoped with pagination → the page is taken from the filtered set

**Envelope round-trip test**, in the style of `internal/robot/envelope_test.go`: the scoped and
the failing responses each serialise a complete `RobotResponse`, with no partial payload
alongside an error.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is a filter and a flag.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the three dispatch branches at `:763-772`, `:1013-1014` and
`:2544-2545`, plus the shared resolution helpers at `:5387-5401` — and the signatures of
`robot.PrintStatusWithOptions`, `robot.PrintDashboard` and `robot.PrintTerse` in
`internal/robot/`, each of which gains an optional session scope. No other robot query is
touched, no pattern or classifier is involved, and nothing outside these three renderings changes
shape.
