title: Put the coordination identity into the environment the panes actually run in
description:
## Outcome

`ntm swarm` puts the coordination identity into the environment its panes actually run in, and
refuses to launch when it cannot. After this bead a pane's shell sees `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED` and
its own `AGENT_NAME` because `ntm` placed them there when it created the session and the pane, not
because the operator happened to export them in the shell that typed the command — and a launch
that cannot guarantee that fails loudly, naming the variable and the pane it could not equip,
before any agent starts work.

## Context

**The two variables gate an external pre-commit hook, and when they are unset it passes
everything.** MCP Agent Mail's reservation guard is the only *enforced* exclusion layer a
shared-tree swarm has: several agents edit one checkout, and the hook is what refuses a commit
over a path another agent holds. When neither `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED` nor `WORKTREES_ENABLED` is
set in the committing shell, the guard exits 0 having read no reservation at all. An unset
variable and a clean commit look identical, so a swarm can run its whole length with the layer
inert and nothing anywhere reports it.

**`ntm` is where this can be fixed because `ntm` is what creates the environment.** The
consuming project has no launcher of its own; `ntm swarm` is what starts the panes. A wrapper
script there was considered and rejected: it is bypassed by running `ntm swarm` directly, which
is the obvious path.

**But the obvious implementation would be wrong, and this is the paragraph that matters.**
Reading `os.Getenv("GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED")` inside `runSwarm` validates the *caller's*
environment, and the caller's environment is not what the panes get. Measured 2026-08-29:

- `internal/tmux/session.go:911` (`CreateSessionWithHistoryLimitContext`, which every
  `CreateSession*` entry point funnels into) creates the session with
  `tmux new-session -d -s <name> -c <dir>` and never passes `-e VAR=value`.
- `internal/tmux/session.go:1365` (`SplitWindowContext`) creates every pane after the first with
  `tmux split-window -t <target> -c <dir> -P -F '#{pane_id}'`, also without `-e`.
- `internal/swarm/pane_launcher.go:236-237` and `:273` "launch" a pane by `SendKeys` into a shell
  that is already running — keystrokes, exactly as a person would type them.
- `internal/tmux/client.go:478` execs the tmux **client** binary without ever setting `cmd.Env`.

So the pane's shell is forked by the tmux **server**. When a server is already running — the
common case, since it is a long-lived daemon that may predate this invocation by days — the new
session inherits *that server's* environment table, not this process's. Nothing in the call path
reads or writes the session environment (`set-environment`, or `-e` on `new-session`).

A check that reads the caller's env would therefore pass while the panes lack the variables, and
fail while they have them. It would be a guard that reports confidently on the wrong thing, which
is worse than the current state: today nobody believes the layer is checked.

**Hence the outcome is propagation first and refusal second.** Set the variables where the pane's
shell will read them, verify, then refuse if not. Validating an environment `ntm` also sets is a
check with a subject; validating one it merely inherits is not.

### Three design points, settled here so nobody reopens them

**1. The two variables live at different scopes, and that decides the mechanism for each.** The
tmux *session* environment is shared by every pane in the session — `set-environment` and
`show-environment` are session-scoped, so a value that must differ per pane cannot live there.
tmux does support a per-pane environment through `-e` on the command that creates the pane
(`new-session -e`, `split-window -e`; both present in the `tmux(1)` of the host's 3.7b and of the
3.5a in `test.Containerfile`). So:

- `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED` is **session-scoped**: pass it as `-e` on `new-session` *and* set it with
  `set-environment -t <session>` so a pane created later still inherits it. It is verified by
  reading it back with `show-environment -t <session>`.
- `AGENT_NAME` is **pane-scoped**: pass it as `-e` on the command that creates that pane. The
  first pane of a session is created by `new-session`, not by `split-window`, so it takes its name
  from `new-session -e` and every later pane from `split-window -e` — a change that only touches
  `split-window` leaves pane 1 unequipped. It cannot be verified with `show-environment`, which
  reads the session table; it is verified as described under Tests.

**2. Where a pane's `AGENT_NAME` comes from: derive it from the pane's own coordinates,
`<session-name>-p<pane-index>`, using the 1-based `PaneSpec.Index` at
`internal/swarm/types.go:79-85`.** Deterministic, distinct by construction across a launch, and
readable in a log next to the pane title. The alternative considered and rejected is reusing MCP
Agent Mail's identity: `internal/agentmail/session.go:96-107` stores exactly one `agent.json` per
**session and project**, so it has no per-pane value to offer and could not supply distinct names
for the panes of one session. Registration-time name generation was rejected for the same reason
plus a second one — it would make a launch refusal depend on a network service being up.

**3. `WORKTREES_ENABLED` is deliberately not set.** The guard passes everything when *neither*
variable is set, so setting `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED` alone is sufficient to arm it. The other
variable declares a different topology — one worktree per agent — and a swarm launched by
`ntm swarm` shares one checkout, so setting it would make the tree describe itself falsely to any
consumer that reads it. Out of scope, stated rather than forgotten.

**`AGENT_NAME` differs per pane and that is the point.** The guard uses it to tell one agent's
reservations from another's, and the tracker's claim guard has the matching defect: `br update
--claim` refuses only when a *different* actor holds the bead, so two panes claiming under one
identity both succeed with no error. A single shared `AGENT_NAME` across panes satisfies a naive
"is it set" check and reintroduces exactly the collision the guard exists to prevent.

**Two refusal points, because the two scopes become knowable at different moments.** The
name-collision and opt-out checks are pure functions of the plan and run in `runSwarm` beside the
existing guards, before anything is created. The session-environment read-back can only happen
after `new-session`, so it runs there and aborts before any pane is launched — no `SendKeys`
reaches a pane of a session that failed verification, and the session created for the failed
launch is torn down rather than left behind.

**Insertion point and conventions, so this does not have to be rediscovered.** `runSwarm` is
`internal/cli/swarm.go:291`. It already carries three inline refusals of this shape —
`--sessions-per-type < 1` at `:325-327`, `--panes-per-session < 0` at `:333-335`, and a grid-size
guard at `:387-393` — all returning `fmt.Errorf` before any side effect and all running before
`discoverProjects` at `:347`. There is no `preflight.go` to extend; the plan-level half belongs
beside those. Robot mode has its own shape: `robot.NewErrorResponse(cause, code, hint)` at
`:354-368`, with the exit contract in `AGENTS.md:314-324` (`0` success, `1` error with
`error_code`, `2` unavailable). For env-var naming, `ntm`'s own knobs are `NTM_<SECTION>_<FIELD>`
(`internal/config/config.go:2794-2884`) while variables belonging to another service are left
unprefixed — `AGENT_MAIL_URL`, `AGENT_MAIL_TOKEN`, `AGENT_MAIL_ENABLED` at `config.go:2801-2809`.
These two belong to the guard, so they take the unprefixed form; the opt-out is `ntm`'s own knob
and takes the prefixed form.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/swarm.go` (the plan-level refusal and the opt-out flag, beside the existing guards
in `runSwarm`), `internal/tmux/session.go` (the `CreateSession*` family around `:886-930` and
`SplitWindowContext` at `:1352-1370`, both gaining an environment parameter or a variant that
takes one), `internal/swarm/orchestrator.go:150-220` (which creates the session and then each
pane, and is where a pane's derived name is passed in), and `internal/swarm/types.go` if the
derived name is carried on `PaneSpec`. Tests in `internal/cli/swarm_test.go`,
`internal/tmux/session_test.go` and `internal/swarm/orchestrator_test.go`. `internal/config/` is
not touched: `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED` and `AGENT_NAME` are not `ntm` config knobs. No change to the
robot envelope's shape, only a new error code within it.

## Budget

- A pane's shell resolves both variables **100%** of the time after a successful launch, verified
  by reading them back from the session environment and from the pane process, never from the
  caller's environment.
- Every pane in a launch has a **distinct** `AGENT_NAME`: collisions across panes stay at **0**.
- The check adds **under 100 ms** to launch: one `show-environment` read per session, not a probe
  of each pane's shell.
- A launch with everything correctly set is unchanged: **zero** new prompts, flags or steps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ntm swarm` sets `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED=1` in the session environment of every session it
  creates, by `new-session -e` plus `set-environment -t <session>`, so a pane created later
  inherits it too — and it survives the pane being forked by a tmux server that was already
  running with neither variable in its own table.
- [ ] `ntm swarm` sets a per-pane `AGENT_NAME` through `-e` on the command that creates the pane:
  `new-session -e` for the first pane of each session, `split-window -e` for every later one. A
  change that equips only the `split-window` path leaves pane 1 unequipped and does not satisfy
  this.
- [ ] The value is `<session-name>-p<PaneSpec.Index>`, and every pane of a launch therefore has a
  **distinct** `AGENT_NAME`. A duplicate is a refusal, not a warning: it defeats both the
  reservation guard and the tracker's claim guard at once.
- [ ] `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED` is **verified after setting**, by reading it back with
  `show-environment -t <session>` — the session's own table, never `os.Getenv` in `ntm`'s process,
  which is the environment the panes do not necessarily get.
- [ ] When verification fails, `ntm swarm` **refuses before any pane is launched**: no `SendKeys`
  reaches a pane of that session, the session created for the failed launch is removed, and the
  message names the variable and the session. The plan-level checks (duplicate name, opt-out)
  refuse earlier still, in `runSwarm` beside the `--sessions-per-type` and `--panes-per-session`
  guards, before anything is created.
- [ ] Robot mode returns a structured error with its own `error_code` and a `hint`, following
  `robot.NewErrorResponse` and the exit contract in `AGENTS.md`; plain mode returns `fmt.Errorf`.
  The two agree on when they fire.
- [ ] The behaviour is **opt-out, not opt-in**: `--no-identity-env` (and `NTM_SWARM_IDENTITY_ENV=0`)
  skips both the propagation and the refusal, and taking it is printed in the launch output rather
  than being silent. A swarm that disables its exclusion layer should have to say it out loud.
- [ ] `WORKTREES_ENABLED` is not set by `ntm swarm`, for the reason in the Context.
- [ ] A launch where everything is already correct behaves exactly as today: no new flag is
  required, no prompt appears, and the existing swarm tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Done when: a pane spawned by `ntm swarm` cannot reach a shell where the reservation guard
  reads as unconfigured, unless the operator explicitly asked for that.

## Tests

- **Unit, table-driven, no tmux.** The plan-level validation factored as its own function and
  called directly, following `TestResolveSwarmInitialPrompt_MutuallyExclusive` at
  `internal/cli/swarm_test.go:101-106`: two panes deriving the same `AGENT_NAME`, a pane whose
  derived name is empty, the opt-out set, and **all correct — which must return no error**. That
  last case is the planted negative; a validator that refuses everything passes the first three.
- **Unit, fake tmux client, argv assertion.** The command recorded for session creation contains
  `-e GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED=1` and `-e AGENT_NAME=<session>-p1`, and the command recorded for the
  second pane contains `-e AGENT_NAME=<session>-p2`. This is what proves pane 1 is equipped by
  `new-session` rather than being forgotten.
- **Unit, `t.Setenv`.** The caller's environment being correct must **not** by itself satisfy the
  check. Set both variables in the test process, arrange a session whose environment lacks them,
  and assert verification still fails. This is the assertion that encodes the whole point of the
  bead, and the obvious wrong implementation passes every other test while failing this one.
- **Integration, real tmux server on a private socket** (`-S`, per the repo's tmux socket guard).
  Launch a session through the changed path and read `GIT_IDENTITY_ENABLED` back with
  `tmux show-environment`. Then repeat against a **pre-existing** server started with a
  deliberately empty environment — that is the case the current code gets wrong, and it is not
  exercised by a test that starts its own fresh server.
- **Integration, per-pane value.** Two panes in one launch resolve two different `AGENT_NAME`
  values, read from the pane's own process rather than from the session table: resolve each pane's
  pid with `display-message -p -t <pane> -F '#{pane_pid}'` and read `/proc/<pid>/environ`. Skip
  with a stated precondition where `/proc` is absent, never a bare "unsupported".
- **Unit.** The opt-out path launches, sets nothing, and says so in the output; and its robot-mode
  counterpart carries the same statement.

## Recovery path

The refusal is a guard in front of an existing function and the propagation is additive: an
environment variable a pane's shell may or may not consult. Pass `--no-identity-env`, or revert
the guard, and `ntm swarm` behaves as it does today. No tmux state is migrated, no config file is
rewritten, and a session created by the changed code is an ordinary tmux session with two extra
environment entries that nothing is required to read.

title: detectAgentTypeFromPane has no pi case, so --assign and --init-prompt skip pi panes
description:
## Outcome

`detectAgentTypeFromPane` recognises a pi pane, so the `--assign` and `--init-prompt` spawn paths
see pi panes as agent panes instead of `unknown`. A pi-only swarm started through either of those
paths reaches its agents, and a pane of a genuinely unrecognised agent still reports `unknown`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ntm spawn <project> --pi=2:<model> --init-prompt "<text>"` (or the `--assign` equivalent), in a
   session whose panes are all pi.
2. The readiness pass that gates those two paths runs
   `readyAgentPanesFromObservation` / `readinessIssuesForAgentPanes`, which classify each pane
   through `detectAgentTypeFromPane` (`internal/cli/activity.go`).
3. Every pi pane classifies as `"unknown"` rather than `pi`, so the pane is not counted as a ready
   agent pane and the prompt is not delivered to it.

Reported 2026-08-24 by the agent implementing `bd-ffv3d`, from reading the code while tracing the
`--prompt` path. **The end-to-end failure has not been observed** — that is the first thing to
establish, because it decides whether this is a live defect or a latent one.

## Context

`bd-gc0` fixed the two tmux-metadata type tables in `internal/robot/robot.go` and the coordinator's
title parser, and `bd-ffv3d` covered the `--prompt` readiness path. `internal/cli/activity.go` has
a **third** type-detection function that neither touched, and it is the one the other two spawn
paths depend on.

This is the same shape as `bd-gc0`: pi's correct behaviour throughout ntm is to have no case and
fall open, and a function that resolves it to `unknown` instead of `pi` replaces falling open with
being invisible. The difference is the consequence — `bd-gc0` caused a pi pane to be treated as
Codex, and this one causes it not to be treated as an agent pane at all.

Whether the third table should be fixed in place, or whether the three should be reconciled behind
one resolver, is a real design question and part of the work rather than settled here. Three
independent tables that disagree about the same pane is how both of these defects happened.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `detectAgentTypeFromPane` returns `pi` for a pane whose process or title says pi, in the
      same title conventions `internal/robot`'s `detectAgentType` accepts after `bd-gc0`
- [ ] A pane of an agent type in no table still resolves to `unknown` — the fix adds a case, it
      does not add a fallback that guesses
- [ ] `readyAgentPanesFromObservation` counts a pi pane as a ready agent pane, and
      `readinessIssuesForAgentPanes` does not report it as an issue purely for being pi
- [ ] The end-to-end claim is settled before the fix is written: either a `--init-prompt` or
      `--assign` spawn onto a pi-only session is shown to skip its panes, or it is shown to work
      and this bead is closed as latent with that evidence recorded
- [ ] Every other agent type these two paths already handle classifies exactly as it does today
- [ ] Done when: a pi-only session started with `--init-prompt` delivers to every pane, and the
      three type-detection sites agree about a pi pane or the code says why they must differ.

## Tests

- **Unit test** — table-driven over `detectAgentTypeFromPane`: a pi pane by process, a pi pane by
  `__pi_<index>` title, one row per other known type, and a pane matching nothing which must
  resolve to `unknown`.
- **Unit test** — `readyAgentPanesFromObservation` and `readinessIssuesForAgentPanes` over an
  observation of pi panes: the panes are counted ready and produce no issue.
- **Regression test** — the same two functions over cc and cod panes, unchanged from today.
- **Consistency test** — one pi pane fixture fed through all three detection sites
  (`internal/cli/activity.go`, `internal/robot/robot.go`, `internal/coordinator/detect_agent_type.go`),
  asserting they agree. This is the test whose absence let the same defect appear twice.

Each assertion must be driven red on purpose before it is trusted.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/activity.go` and its tests. `internal/robot/robot.go` and
`internal/coordinator/detect_agent_type.go` are read for consistency and are **not** changed —
`bd-gc0` settled both, and the consistency test above pins them rather than editing them. No robot
response schema changes and no spawn behaviour outside the two named paths.

## Recovery path

Detection logic with no persisted state and no schema change, so reverting the commit fully
restores the previous behaviour. If the end-to-end claim turns out to be false, the correct outcome
is closing this bead with the evidence rather than landing a fix for a defect that does not occur.
close_reason: Implemented in 9e16209c. Two-line production change adding the tmux.AgentPi case to detectAgentTypeFromPane, plus 105 lines of test. The end-to-end claim the bead demanded was settled rather than assumed: TestSendInitPromptDeliversToPiPanes drives sendInitPromptToReadyAgentsWith, the function --init-prompt calls, over a real pi observation; it failed with 'no agent panes were observed' before the fix. Verified independently by mutation: removing the case again turns that test and both TestDetectAgentTypeFromPane pi rows red. internal/cli green under -short.

title: Dispatch gate withholds work from a pane whose scrollback holds a stale error
description:
## Outcome

The coordinator's dispatch gate stops withholding work from a pane whose only sign of trouble is
an error string left in its scrollback. The gate reads a verdict that carries the live-tail and
progress guard, so the fix landed in `bd-j5cdo` reaches the surface that acts on it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an agent pane of a type with no actively-working short-circuit in the static detector —
   gemini, cursor, windsurf, aider, ollama, or a pane classified `unknown`.
2. Let it emit a transient error line, then let it recover and keep producing output.
3. Ask the coordinator for assignment candidates while the pane is working.
4. The pane is skipped: it is not offered work for as long as the offending line stays inside the
   static scan window.

Measured 2026-08-23, after `bd-j5cdo` landed the live-tail plus progress guard on the robot
classifier.

## Context

`bd-j5cdo` fixed the robot classifier: an error pattern matching outside the live tail no longer
produces `error` while the pane is demonstrably progressing. Verified there by breaking each
guard and watching the tests go red.

**The coordinator does not read that classifier for its status.** `resultFromPaneObservation`
(`internal/coordinator/monitor.go:182`) sets `Status: mapStatusToRobotState(current.Status.State)`
— the verdict of the *static* detector in `internal/status`. Lines `195-202` do call the robot
classifier, but assign only `result.Velocity`; there is no `Status` override. Compare
`GetAgentStatus` (`monitor.go:110-114`) and `GetAgentStatusWithOutput` (`:151-155`), which both
carry `if activity.State == robot.StateError { … }` and do override.

That path is the live one: `SessionCoordinator.updateAgentStatesContext`
(`internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:628`) calls it. `GetAllAgentStatuses` and
`GetAgentStatusWithOutput` have no callers in the tree at all, so fixing them would fix nothing.

**What acts on it, and what does not** — established by reading the consumers rather than
assuming:

- **Dispatch gating — yes.** `getAssignmentCandidates` (`internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:403`)
  skips any agent whose `Status` is `robot.StateError`. A working pane is withheld from
  assignment.
- **The `agent.error` event — yes** (`coordinator.go:775`), reaching webhooks, `internal/notify`
  and the attention feed (`internal/robot/attention_feed.go:3140`, `ActionRequired`,
  `SeverityError`). A false alarm rather than a destructive act.
- **The digest** — display only (`internal/coordinator/digest.go:109`).
- **Restart — no.** The resilience restart path runs on `internal/health` plus PID liveness;
  `internal/health` does not import `robot` and holds no `StateError` reference. The static
  verdict never reaches a restart decision, which bounds how much this costs.

**The obvious fix is the wrong one, and this is the part worth reading before starting.** Adding
the same override `GetAgentStatus` carries would change nothing here: that override is one-way —
it escalates to `StateError`, it never clears one. The defect is a *false* error coming out of the
static detector, so what is needed is the robot verdict being able to **downgrade** a static
`StateError`, which is a different change from the symmetry argument it looks like.

**Which panes are exposed.** In `internal/status/unified.go`, `DetectErrorInOutput` (~`:204`) runs
before the `StateWorking` branch (~`:218`). Claude, Codex and pi have earlier actively-working
short-circuits (~`:129`, `:145`, `:174`), and an idle pane at a prompt is rescued at `:186`. Every
other type is exposed. The window is bounded: the static scan is the last 50 lines
(`internal/status/errors.go:96`), so what is exposed is the band between the robot classifier's
width-adaptive live tail and that 50-line bound — narrow, and not empty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A progressing pane of an exposed type (gemini, cursor, windsurf, aider, ollama, unknown)
      with a stale error outside the live tail is offered work by `getAssignmentCandidates`
      (`internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:403`)
- [ ] The same pane with a *current* error in the live tail is still withheld, and still emits
      `agent.error` (`coordinator.go:775`)
- [ ] A pane that is genuinely stuck — a stale error and no output growth between captures — is
      still withheld: the fix must not turn the gate off, only stop it firing on recovered panes
- [ ] `resultFromPaneObservation` (`internal/coordinator/monitor.go:182`) reaches its `Status`
      through a verdict that carries the live-tail and progress guard, and the code says which
      classifier decides
- [ ] The robot verdict can DOWNGRADE a static `StateError`, not only escalate to one — asserted
      by a test, because the one-way override is the trap this bead exists to avoid
- [ ] Claude, Codex and pi panes classify exactly as they do today — their short-circuits already
      rescue them, so their behaviour is a regression surface, not a target
- [ ] No additional tmux capture per coordinator tick: the robot classifier is already called on
      this path for `Velocity`, so the verdict costs no new I/O
- [ ] The comment at `internal/status/unified.go:190-203` is updated to match whatever this bead
      makes true
- [ ] Done when: a fixture pane of an exposed type, progressing with `invalid_api_key` five lines
      back, appears in the assignment candidates, and the same pane with the match in its live
      tail does not.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, over stubbed pane observations so no tmux server is needed, in the
convention of `internal/robot/activity_test.go` and the coordinator's own tests:

- exposed type, stale error, progressing → candidate, no `agent.error`
- exposed type, live-tail error → withheld, `agent.error` emitted
- exposed type, stale error, no growth → withheld (the stuck pane)
- claude / codex / pi, each shape → unchanged from today (regression)
- the downgrade path directly: a static `StateError` plus a robot verdict of working → the result
  is working, asserted at the function that decides it

**Regression test** that `getAssignmentCandidates` still skips a genuinely errored agent, so the
gate is not quietly disabled by this change.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the surface is a classification hand-off between two
existing components.

## Blast radius

`internal/coordinator/monitor.go` — `resultFromPaneObservation` (`:182`) and its use of the robot
classifier at `:195-202` — and the comment at `internal/status/unified.go:190-203`. The static
detector's own logic, the robot classifier landed by `bd-j5cdo`, the error pattern tables and the
restart machinery are **read, not changed**. `getAssignmentCandidates` (`coordinator.go:403`) and
the `agent.error` emission (`:775`) keep their current conditions; what changes is the verdict
they are handed.
close_reason: Implemented in 672f8877. resolveStatus lets the robot verdict downgrade a static StateError while keeping it for a live-tail error and a stuck pane; robotStateHealthy recomputes Healthy from the resolved verdict. Verified by mutation: neutering the downgrade turns TestResolveStatus red on four rows. Scoped suites green (internal/coordinator, internal/status). The withholding of stalled and unknown panes is preserved by the pre-existing Healthy and StateUnknown conditions in getAssignmentCandidates.

title: pi panes are reported as codex by the robot state surfaces
description:
## Outcome

A `pi` pane is reported as `pi` by the robot state surfaces, and a pane that cannot be
classified is reported as `unknown` rather than as some other agent. `pi` gains the cases it is
missing in the two tmux-metadata type tables, and content-based detection stops letting a bare
word match for one agent win over a specific header match for another. After this lands, no
Codex-specific composer check, exit ritual or rate-limit accounting is applied to a pi pane.

## Context

Measured 2026-08-24 on `v1.26.0-36-gfd827f46`, on a two-pane swarm spawned with
`ntm spawn llmux --label ticktest --pi=2:deepseek-v4-pro-high`. Late in the run,
`ntm --robot-is-working <session>` returned `agent_type: "cod"` with `confidence: 0.5` for both
panes, while tmux reported the truth plainly:

    %314 pi llmux--ticktest__pi_1_deepseek-v4-pro-high
    %315 pi llmux--ticktest__pi_2_deepseek-v4-pro-high

Earlier in the same session's life the same surface reported them as `pi`, so this is a state the
panes drift into, not a constant.

Two independent gaps combine. First, the tmux-metadata hint collapses to unknown: `paneAgentType`
(`internal/robot/robot.go:6147-6152`) calls `agentTypeString` (`robot.go:6118-6144`), whose
switch has **no case for pi at all** — it lists claude, codex, gemini, antigravity, grok, cursor,
windsurf, aider, opencode, ollama and user — so a correctly-tracked pi pane is discarded to
`"unknown"`. Its fallback `detectAgentType(pane.Title)` (`robot.go:3777-3824`) has no pi case
either, in neither the substring block nor the short-form block, despite the pane titles here
following exactly the `__<type>_<index>` convention that block parses.

Second, with the hint gone, `ParseWithHint` (`internal/agent/parser.go:35-49`) falls through to
content-based `DetectAgentType` (`parser.go:67-99`), whose checks run in priority order: Claude
header, then `codContextPattern`, then `codHeaderPattern`, and only **then** `piHeaderPattern`.
`codHeaderPattern` is `(?i)\b(codex|openai|gpt-\d)\b` (`internal/agent/patterns.go:251`) — a bare
case-insensitive word match anywhere in captured pane content. `piHeaderPattern`
(`patterns.go:267`) is specific and correct, and never reached once the bare match fires. The
codebase itself describes pi as an OpenAI-compatible client (`internal/agent/types.go:20`), so
the word that trips the earlier pattern is one a pi pane is unusually likely to print.

The observed `confidence: 0.5` corroborates the mechanism rather than merely being consistent
with it. `calculateConfidence` (`parser.go:535-575`) starts at 0.5 and adds +0.25 for extracted
context-remaining, +0.05 for tokens used, up to +0.3 for work indicators and +0.2 for limit
indicators, subtracting 0.3 only when the type stayed unknown. A header-word match with no other
Codex-specific signal present lands on the unmodified base, which is exactly what was measured —
pi's own status line (`0.0%/1.0M (auto)`) does not match `codContextPattern`'s
`\d+%\s*context\s*left`, so the +0.25 was never available.

`cod` is not a fallback: nothing defaults an unclassified pane to it. Elsewhere the default is
`unknown` (`robot.go:3823`, the `agentTypeString` default case,
`internal/coordinator/detect_agent_type.go:44`). This is a real detection outcome from a
wrongly-prioritised pattern, which is worse than a default, because a default is recognisable as
one.

What makes it consequential is that pi's correct behaviour throughout ntm is to have no case and
fall open, and being misread replaces falling open with the wrong agent's ritual:

- **Composer readiness.** `composerMarkerForAgent` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2203-2226`) has no
  pi case, so pi correctly reaches the documented fail-open verdict `VerdictNoClassifier`
  (`session.go:2333-2340`). Misread as cod, the pane is checked for the Codex marker `›` and the
  placeholder `Ask Codex` — text a pi pane never renders — so a path that always passed becomes
  one that can never positively confirm readiness.
- **Exit and restart.** `exitAgent` (`internal/robot/exit_sequences.go:29-38`) sends pi to
  `exitUnknown`, a Ctrl+C fallback. Misread as cod, it runs `exitCodex` and types Codex's
  `/exit` slash-command ritual into a pi pane.
- **Rate-limit accounting.** `internal/robot/health_oauth.go:164` and
  `internal/scheduler/caps.go:249, 288, 356, 414` gate Codex-only throttling on
  `agentType == "cod"`, pulling a misread pi pane into cooldown accounting it does not belong to.

The defect also propagates outward silently: `bin/swarm-tick` in the `llm-workflow` repo prints
the agent type this surface reports, so its output labelled both panes `[cod]` while faithfully
relaying what it was told.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn a pi swarm: `ntm spawn <project> --label <label> --pi=2:<model>`, in a repository whose
   sources or output contain the literal word `openai`, `codex`, or `gpt-<digit>`. The repo used
   here, `llmux`, is an OpenAI-compatible proxy and carries `openai` or `gpt-N` in three Go
   files.
2. Immediately run `ntm --robot-is-working <session>` and note that `agent_type` reads `pi`.
3. Give the panes work that causes one of those words to appear in visible pane output.
4. Run `ntm --robot-is-working <session>` again and observe `agent_type: "cod"` with
   `confidence: 0.5`.
5. Confirm the truth independently:
   `tmux list-panes -t <session>: -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_current_command} #{pane_title}'` reports
   `pi` for both the process and the title.

The step-3 trigger is inference, not established fact: the mechanism was traced through the
patterns and the confidence arithmetic, but the specific line of pane text that matched was not
captured before the session was destroyed. Confirming or refuting that trigger is part of the
work, and the fix should not be written to assume it if a capture shows otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agentTypeString` returns `pi` for a pane whose tracked type is pi, instead of `unknown`.
- [ ] `detectAgentType(title)` recognises the `__pi_<index>` title convention, in both its
      substring and short-form paths.
- [ ] With the hint deliberately unavailable, content whose only agent-identifying token is the
      bare word `openai` no longer classifies as `cod`. It classifies as `pi` when a pi header is
      present, and as `unknown` when nothing specific matches.
- [ ] A specific header match outranks a bare word match regardless of which agent each belongs
      to. Ordering `piHeaderPattern` ahead of `codHeaderPattern` satisfies this bead but is not
      sufficient on its own if the ordering merely moves the collision to the next pair.
- [ ] Genuine Codex panes still classify as `cod`, with no regression in their confidence values.
- [ ] No Codex-specific composer marker, exit ritual, or rate-limit accounting is reachable for a
      pane whose process is pi. Assert this at the branch, not only at the reported type.
- [ ] Done when: a pi pane running for the length of a real swarm reports `pi` on every sampling
      of `--robot-is-working`, and a pane of an unrecognised agent reports `unknown` rather than
      any specific agent name.

## Tests

- **Unit test** — table-driven over `DetectAgentType`, with one row per agent and one row per
  known collision: pi content containing `openai`, pi content containing `gpt-4`, Codex content
  containing a pi-like status line, and content matching nothing. Assert both the resolved type
  and that unmatched content resolves to unknown rather than to any named agent.
- **Unit test** — `agentTypeString` and `detectAgentType` over pi panes and pi-formatted titles,
  asserting `pi` rather than `unknown`.
- **Unit test** — `calculateConfidence` for a bare-header match with no supporting signal,
  pinning the 0.5 base so a future change to the additive terms does not quietly make a weak
  match look strong.
- **Unit test** — `exitAgent` and `composerMarkerForAgent` given a pi pane, asserting the
  fail-open and Ctrl+C paths are chosen and the Codex paths are not.
- **Golden test** — a captured pi pane transcript, checked into testdata, classified as `pi`.
  This is the artefact whose absence made the original trigger unprovable, so producing it is
  part of the fix.

Every new assertion must be driven red on purpose before it is trusted: a table-driven detector
test that passes against the current code is testing nothing this bead is about.

## Blast radius

`internal/agent/parser.go` and `internal/agent/patterns.go` for detection order and the pi
pattern, `internal/robot/robot.go` for the two type tables, plus their tests and one new
testdata capture. `internal/coordinator/detect_agent_type.go` is read to keep the two title
parsers consistent and may gain a pi case. No robot response schema changes: `agent_type`
already carries `pi` as a legal value, so no consumer needs updating, and nothing about
reservations, panes or sessions is touched.

## Recovery path

Detection logic only, with no persisted state and no schema change, so reverting the commit fully
restores the previous behaviour. The one caveat to record at merge time: any consumer that
learned to work around panes being reported as `cod` would need its workaround removed in the
same change rather than after it.
close_reason: Implemented in a41253c2, merged as 52a87983. piHeaderPattern now checked first in DetectAgentType and 'openai' removed from codHeaderPattern; pi cases added to agentTypeString, robot detectAgentType and the coordinator title parser. New tests verified red against origin/main (DetectAgentType returned cod, want pi) before the fix. Scoped suites green: internal/agent, internal/coordinator, internal/robot.

Both were observed in the same run on 2026-08-24. They are not blocking each other and the code paths differ (readiness classification versus DetectAgentType), but adding pi to agentTypeString in internal/robot/robot.go:6118-6144 plausibly affects both, so whoever takes one should read the other before starting.

title: send --clear-input refuses on a placeholder, with no way through
description:
## Outcome

`ntm send --clear-input` distinguishes a composer that holds text from one showing a placeholder,
and it never refuses a send on the strength of rendered text alone. When it cannot tell, it says
so and offers a way through instead of a wall.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn a Claude Code pane and send it a prompt, so its composer renders the previous prompt as
   greyed placeholder text — `❯ check ready pool again for new work` in the observed case.
2. `ntm send <session> --pane=%NN --clear-input '<new prompt>'`.
3. Observe the refusal:
   `Error: COMPOSER_NOT_CLEARED: pane 1.8 composer still holds text after the clear sequence;
   inspect with --robot-tail before resending`.
4. Confirm the composer was empty the whole time: `Escape`, `C-u` and `Enter` all leave the text
   untouched, while `tmux send-keys -t %NN -l "X"` replaces the entire line — which a real
   composer holding content would not do.

## Context

The check reads rendered pane text, and Claude Code renders its placeholder in the same cell
region as real input. So the guard cannot separate *the composer holds content* from *the
composer is empty and the UI is showing what was last sent* — and its refusal is therefore not
evidence that a composer is dirty.

The refusal is also terminal: there is no `--force` and no override, so the operator's only route
is to abandon `ntm send` for that pane and go to raw tmux:

```sh
tmux load-buffer -b rw1 <prompt-file>
tmux paste-buffer -p -b rw1 -t %NN   # -p is required: bracketed paste
tmux send-keys -t %NN Enter
```

That is what happened for every Claude dispatch of an eleven-hour unattended run after the first
refusal. The cost is not the keystrokes — it is that the delivery path with the safety check in it
was replaced by one with no checks at all, for the rest of the night, on the pane type the
check was written for.

**The design point worth keeping.** A guard that cannot distinguish two states should not resolve
them in the direction that blocks work while claiming certainty. Either the check gains a signal
that separates placeholder from content, or the refusal becomes advisory with a documented
override.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a Claude Code pane whose composer is empty and showing placeholder text,
      `--clear-input` sends, and does not refuse
- [ ] Given a pane whose composer genuinely holds typed text, `--clear-input` still clears it, or
      still refuses — the existing protection is not traded away to fix the false positive
- [ ] Both directions are asserted against captured pane text, so the fix cannot be "stop
      checking"
- [ ] When the two cases cannot be told apart for a given agent type, the refusal names that as
      the reason and points at an override rather than reading as a dirty composer
- [ ] An override exists — a `--force`, or an equivalent — so an operator is never left with raw
      tmux as the only route
- [ ] The error text stops asserting `composer still holds text` when that is not established
- [ ] Done when: the placeholder case from the reproduction sends successfully, and a pane with
      real typed content in its composer still does not get silently overwritten.

## Tests

- **Unit:** over the composer-state classifier, with captured pane text for each case — empty with
  placeholder, empty with no placeholder, holding typed content, and mid-render.
- **Integration:** against a live Claude Code pane in each of the two states, since the whole
  defect is that rendered text under-determines the state.
- **Regression:** the exact placeholder string from the reproduction must not produce
  `COMPOSER_NOT_CLEARED`.
- **Mutation, before it is trusted:** make the classifier answer "empty" unconditionally and
  confirm the typed-content test fails. A one-directional test passes against a check that has
  simply been switched off, which is the easiest wrong fix here.

## Blast radius

The composer-clearing check behind `ntm send --clear-input` and its error text, plus the flag
surface if an override is added, and their tests. Prompt delivery itself, pane targeting by id,
and every other `ntm send` path are read but not changed.

title: Same-intent assign replay is refused with PANE_BUSY: the durable prior record is not found
description:
## Outcome

A same-intent `ntm assign` replay reaches its durable prior record and bypasses the busy-pane
preflight, instead of being refused with `PANE_BUSY`. `TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight`
passes for the reason it was written, and a genuinely different intent against a busy pane is still
refused.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build with the toolchain the module pins (see the note at the end — a mismatched `go` fails in a
   way that looks like a code defect).
2. `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1 -run TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight`
3. The test drives its fake agent pane to `state=working` on purpose and asserts it — that assertion
   passes. It then issues the identical `assign` invocation a second time and expects the replay to
   go through.
4. It fails at `internal/cli/assign_test.go:4134`:

        same-intent replay failed: code=1 stderr="" error=&{Code:PANE_BUSY
        Message:pane 1.0 is busy (state: working), use --force to override}

Measured 2026-08-25 on the merge of `bd-sr2sg`. Before that merge this test failed earlier, at
`PANE_AGENT_DEAD`, because its fixture presented a bare shell; the fixture repair is what let the
test reach this point for the first time. **So this defect has never been observed working**, and
"it used to pass" must not be assumed.

## Context

`runDirectAssign` skips the whole preflight — including the busy-pane refusal — when the invocation
replays a prior intent:

    sameIntent := prior != nil && prior.IdempotencyKey == idempotencyKey   // assign.go:5841
    executeBeforePreflight := sameIntent || activeDifferentIntent          // assign.go:5849

The `PANE_BUSY` refusal lives inside that skipped preflight (`assign.go:5910-5916`), gated on
`!paneObservation.SafeToDispatch() && !opts.Force`.

The key is derived in `snapshotDirectAssignmentIntent` (`assign.go:5687-5710`) from the session, the
bead id, the pane id and `PromptSHA256` of the prompt source, plus a `cleared-generation` part when
one is supplied. **The test passes byte-identical arguments on both calls** — same `baseArgs` slice,
same session, same `--pane`, same `--beads`, same `--prompt` — so every input to the key is the same
on the replay.

That narrows the failure: if the key inputs are identical and `sameIntent` was nevertheless false,
then `prior` was nil, i.e. the first assignment's durable record was not found when the second
invocation looked for it. The two invocations are separate processes
(`runDirectAssignCLIProcess`), so the record has to survive a process boundary — which is precisely
what the test's name claims to cover. **Where the record is written and where the replay reads it
back is the thing to establish first**; the above is a narrowing, not a diagnosis, and the reader
should confirm `prior` is actually nil before assuming it.

Ruled out already: the prompt is passed explicitly, so `explicitPrompt` is true on both calls and no
template rendering can perturb the hash; and `clearedGeneration` is not supplied by this path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `go test ./internal/cli/ -count=1 -run TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight`
      passes, with the test's existing assertions unchanged — in particular the one that requires the
      pane to be `state=working` before the replay
- [ ] The cause is stated in the commit body as an observed fact: whether `prior` was nil, and if so
      why the record was absent. A fix that makes the test green without naming the cause is not
      acceptable here, because the test has never been seen passing
- [ ] A replay carrying a genuinely different intent against a busy pane is still refused with
      `PANE_BUSY` — the bypass must not widen into "assign never checks busy again"
- [ ] The two receipts remain byte-identical across the replay, which the test already asserts
- [ ] `--force` behaviour is unchanged
- [ ] No change to the idempotency key derivation unless the key is shown to be the cause, in which
      case the change is called out explicitly: the key is persisted, so altering it invalidates
      every stored assignment record

## Tests

- **Unit test** — `sameIntent` resolution given a stored prior with a matching key: assert
  `executeBeforePreflight` is true and the busy preflight is not consulted.
- **Unit test** — the same with a differing key: assert the preflight runs and `PANE_BUSY` is
  returned for a busy pane.
- **Integration test** — the durable record written by one process is read back by another, which is
  the boundary the existing test crosses and the one no unit test covers.
- **Regression test** — the existing `TestDirectAssignCLIReplayIsDurableAndBypassesChangedPreflight`
  is the acceptance test; it must pass without weakening any assertion.

Drive each new assertion red on purpose. The existing test is already red, which is the one piece of
red-first evidence that comes for free here.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/assign.go` around the intent snapshot (`:5687-5714`), the `sameIntent` resolution
(`:5841-5849`) and wherever the durable assignment record is written and read; plus the assignment
store under `internal/assignment/`. The fake-agent fixtures repaired by `bd-sr2sg` are **not** to be
touched — weakening them would hide this defect again, which is how it stayed invisible until now.

## Recovery path

CLI control flow plus, possibly, a persisted record's lifetime. If the fix changes what is written to
the assignment store, reverting the commit leaves records written in the meantime on disk; they are
read by the same code that wrote them before, so no migration is required, but say so at merge time.
If the idempotency key derivation changes, stored records keyed the old way stop matching and every
replay becomes a first attempt — recoverable, but it must be a stated decision rather than a side
effect.

## Note on the toolchain

A `/usr/bin/go` tagged `go1.26.6-X:nodwarf5` cannot reuse a build cache produced by a plain
`go1.26.6`; it fails with `compile: version "go1.26.6" does not match go tool version`, which reads
like a defect in the code under test. Build with the toolchain the module pins.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #5 (merged as d88a47d3): IsolateUserConfigProcess re-randomized HOME in every process, so the dispatching and replaying processes of the durability test never shared a config root and the prior assignment record was unreachable. The isolator now honours NTM_TEST_TMUX_ENV_OWNED only when TMUX_TMPDIR proves ownership. assign.go and the idempotency key were not touched.

title: assign verifies prompt delivery, not only the claim
description:
## Outcome

`ntm assign` reports delivery, not just the claim: its result says whether the prompt text actually reached the target pane, and a claim-landed/prompt-missing outcome is a visible failure, never a silent success.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed 2026-08-31 (orchestrator survey, ntm defects):

1. `ntm assign --beads aub-eqpk --pane %647` — the atomic tracker claim landed, the command printed nothing to stdout, and the prompt never appeared in the pane; the operator completed delivery with a separate `ntm send`.
2. Same shape earlier via the loop's heartbeat against the codex boot-modal pane: claim per heartbeat, no prompt ever rendered.

## Context

Assign is two operations — claim the bead, deliver the brief — and only the first is verified. The failure mode it produces is the worst bead state there is: owned and inert, invisible to re-dispatch because the claim exists, worked by nobody because the brief never arrived. bd-ljd covers spawn-time marching-orders confirmation; this is the assign verb. The swarm side (swarm-dispatch not counting unconfirmed deliveries) is filed separately in llm-workflow; both need ntm to expose the delivery fact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Assign's robot result carries a per-assignment `delivered` verdict based on a post-send receipt check (the SEND surface's receipt plus a fresh capture containing a delivery marker), not on send-command acceptance.
- [ ] When delivery fails after the claim landed, the result says so explicitly (error_code distinguishing claim_ok_delivery_failed), and the human output is non-empty.
- [ ] `--json` and plain output both carry the verdict; exit code is non-zero on any failed delivery.
- [ ] Done when: assigning to a pane whose agent cannot receive input (modal-wedged fixture) returns claim_ok_delivery_failed instead of silence.

## Tests

- Integration: assign against a test pane with input blocked asserts the failure verdict and exit code; against a healthy pane asserts delivered=true and the prompt visible in capture.

## Blast radius

Confined to ntm's assign command path (delivery verification and result envelope) and its tests. The claim protocol itself is untouched; no beads schema change.

title: Install a repo-owned pre-commit hook that flushes the bead export, so a local bead reaches the commit
description:
## Outcome

A commit made in this repository cannot leave the bead database and the tracked
`.beads/issues.jsonl` disagreeing: a `pre-commit` hook lives in the repository, is installed by a
documented one-line command, runs `br sync --flush-only` and stages the tracked `.beads` JSONL. A
bead created locally reaches the committed export on the next commit instead of existing only in a
git-ignored database on one machine.

## Outcome, restated as the failure it removes

On 2026-08-26 the tracked export was three beads behind the live database: `bd-xox` and `bd-f6e`
were closed and `bd-3nv` claimed with none of it exported, and — worse — **`bd-hf1` and `bd-jyy`
had never reached the committed export at all.** A clone of this repository did not contain those
two beads in any form. They were recovered only because a session ran `git status` in the main tree
and saw the file dirty.

## Context

`.beads/beads.db` is git-ignored (`.beads/.gitignore:2`) and `.beads/issues.jsonl` is tracked
(`.beads/.gitignore:42-46` documents exactly that split). The export is therefore the only copy of
the tracker that travels with the repository, and nothing in this repository produces it.

**What is supposed to produce it.** `CONTRIBUTING.md:39-46` describes a generated `pre-commit` hook
that runs `br sync --flush-only` and stages every tracked `.beads` JSONL. That hook is not checked
in, and on this machine it does not exist and could not run if it did:

- `ls .git/hooks` in this repository contains only `*.sample` files — no hook was ever generated
  here.
- `core.hooksPath` is set **globally** to `~/.config/git/hooks` (from
  `~/.config/git/config`), a directory holding a single `commit-msg` symlink. A global
  `core.hooksPath` overrides every repository's own `.git/hooks`, so even a generated hook would be
  bypassed.

**Every sibling repository already solves this the same way, and this one is the outlier.** `kernl`,
`llm-workflow` and `transaction-authorizer` each set a **repository-local** `core.hooksPath` to
their own tracked `.githooks/` directory; `br sync --status` in each reports `In sync`. This
repository is the only one of the four with beads and no repo-local hooks path.

**CI cannot be the gate here, and it is worth saying why so nobody builds it.** A CI job has the
JSONL and not the database — the database is git-ignored and never leaves the machine — so there is
nothing for CI to compare the export against. The check has to run where both halves exist, which
is a local pre-commit hook.

**The trap this bead must not fall into.** A repository-local `core.hooksPath` **overrides** the
global one rather than adding to it, and the global one is what installs the `commit-msg`
attribution guard. Pointing this repository at its own `.githooks/` without carrying that hook over
would silently disable that guard for every commit made here — trading a tracker defect for a
publishing defect, which is worse and quieter. Whatever this bead installs must keep `commit-msg`
working, and prove it.

**`br sync --flush-only` is the right command and is safe by construction.** Its own help states it
never executes git commands and never auto-commits, writes only inside `.beads/`, and uses an atomic
temp-file-then-rename. Staging is therefore the hook's job, not the tool's.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a clean checkout of this repository: `br create "throwaway probe" -t chore`.
2. `git status --porcelain .beads` — the export is unchanged; the new bead exists only in the
   git-ignored database.
3. Commit anything at all: `git commit --allow-empty -m "probe"`.
4. `git status --porcelain .beads` again.

**Expected:** the commit carries the refreshed `issues.jsonl`, and the new bead is in it.

**Observed:** `.beads/issues.jsonl` is untouched by the commit and the bead is absent from it. It
stays absent until someone runs `br sync --flush-only` by hand and commits the result, which is how
two beads went unexported for weeks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A tracked `.githooks/pre-commit` runs `br sync --flush-only` and then `git add`s the tracked
      files under `.beads/`, and exits non-zero if the flush itself fails
- [ ] A tracked `.githooks/commit-msg` preserves the attribution guard that the global hooks path
      provides today, so pointing this repository at its own hooks directory does not remove it
- [ ] A documented one-line install step sets the repository-local `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`,
      named in `CONTRIBUTING.md` in place of the description of the generated hook that does not
      exist
- [ ] After installing, `br create` followed by any commit leaves `git status --porcelain .beads`
      empty and the new bead present in the committed `issues.jsonl` — the reproduction above,
      inverted
- [ ] A commit whose message would fail the attribution guard is still refused after the install,
      proven by attempting one
- [ ] The hook works from a linked worktree created by `scripts/worktree.sh new`, where `.beads/`
      holds a `redirect` rather than a database
- [ ] Done when: a bead created in this repository reaches the committed export on the next commit
      without anyone remembering to run a command.

## Tests

- **Integration (shell, one-shot, in a scratch clone):** the reproduction inverted — create a bead,
  commit, assert the bead's id appears in the committed `issues.jsonl` and that
  `git status --porcelain .beads` is empty afterwards. This is the test that would have caught the
  original defect.
- **Integration (shell):** a commit made from a worktree created by `scripts/worktree.sh new`, where
  `.beads/redirect` stands in for the database, asserting the same two things. The redirect path is
  where a hook that assumes a local database silently does nothing.
- **Integration (shell), the guard-preservation case:** attempt a commit whose message trips the
  attribution guard after the install and assert it is refused. Without this the bead can be
  "finished" while having disabled a gate nobody would notice for weeks.
- **Not owed:** a CI check comparing database and export. CI has only the export, so the comparison
  is not expressible there — see the Context.

## Recovery path

`git config --unset core.hooksPath` in this repository returns it to the global hooks path and to
today's behaviour: no flush on commit, and the attribution guard supplied globally. The tracked
`.githooks/` directory can stay in place while uninstalled, so the revert is one command and loses
no work.

## Blast radius

Two new tracked files under `.githooks/`, one install line in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and one
repository-local git config setting. No Go code, no CI workflow, no change to `scripts/worktree.sh`,
and no change to how `br` is invoked anywhere else in the repository.
close_reason: verified at 61f677f0: make build green, and scripts/test_beads_hook.sh 12/12. Mutation independently re-run by the orchestrator against a COMMITTED mutation (the suite clones from HEAD, so a working-tree edit is invisible to it): removing the 'git add -f' staging loop turns 4 cases red, naming the unstaged export and the bead missing from the committed JSONL. Removing 'br sync --flush-only' leaves all 12 green - br auto-flushes on mutation, so that half is unguarded; filed as a follow-up, not a blocker, since the bead's outcome is proven by the staging half. PR #22 merged.

title: Operator cannot reserve or release files when a session's Agent Mail identity is missing
description:
## Outcome

An operator can release or renew a file reservation in a session whose coordinator identity is
missing, instead of being refused with an error that names no recovery. Either `lock`, `unlock`,
`locks force-release` and `locks renew` grow the same identity-resolution fallbacks the mail
commands already have, or they self-heal the missing identity the way `mail send` self-heals its
own, or at minimum the error names the command that would repair it. Reservations stop being
strandable by a failure the operator never saw happen.

## Context

Measured 2026-08-24 on `v1.26.0-36-gfd827f46`. A two-pane `pi` swarm was spawned with
`ntm spawn llmux --label ticktest --pi=2:deepseek-v4-pro-high`. The pane agents reserved files
through Agent Mail successfully — eight live exclusive reservations, each carrying a bead id as
its reason — and `ntm locks list llmux --all-agents` read them back correctly. But every
operator-side write failed:

    $ ntm lock llmux--ticktest "internal/route/stress_test.go" --reason "..." --ttl 10m
    Error: session 'llmux--ticktest' has no Agent Mail identity

    $ ntm unlock llmux--ticktest --all
    Error: session 'llmux--ticktest' has no Agent Mail identity

The consequence is not cosmetic. When that swarm was shut down, nine reservations were left
holding paths with no owner alive and no command able to release them; they expired on their own
roughly an hour later. An advisory system whose reservations can only be cleared by waiting is
one that quietly teaches operators to ignore it.

The two write paths are backed by different stores, which is why one worked and the other did
not. Per-pane identities live in `agent_registry.json` (`internal/agentmail/session.go:405-419`),
populated by `registerSpawnedAgents` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:4356`). The session-wide coordinator
identity is a separate `agent.json` under
`~/.config/ntm/sessions/<session>/<projectSlug>/` (`internal/agentmail/session.go:18-22, 96-108`),
created only by `RegisterSessionAgent` (`session.go:285-343`) through the wrapper at
`spawn.go:4307-4340`. `runLock` (`internal/cli/lock.go:85-93`), `runUnlock`
(`internal/cli/unlock.go:105-113`), `locks force-release` (`internal/cli/locks.go:1192-1200`) and
`locks renew` (`locks.go:1371-1379`) all read that second file and hard-fail when it is absent.
`locks list` never asks for an identity, which is why the read path was unaffected.

Two things make the failure invisible rather than merely inconvenient. First, the two
registrations are called back to back at every spawn/add/adopt site, but only the pane one has a
reconciliation path for a busy server (`spawn.go:4453`, listing agents and matching by program
and model); `RegisterSessionAgent` makes one unretried call and bubbles any error up. Second, the
caller prints that error only `if !IsJSONOutput()` (`spawn.go:4335-4340`), so under `--json`
nothing reports it and the spawn response does not reflect it. A registration race at spawn — N
pane registrations and one coordinator registration arriving together — would therefore kill the
coordinator identity silently while the individually-reconciled pane identities survive, which
matches exactly what was observed.

There is no operator escape hatch today. The mail commands resolve an identity through three
fallbacks — an `--agent` flag, a `TMUX_PANE` lookup in the pane registry, then `AGENT_NAME`
(`internal/cli/mail.go:687-720`). None of that chain exists for the lock commands, which accept
no `--agent` flag and read no environment variable. The only way found to regenerate the missing
file is as a side effect of `ntm add`, `ntm adopt`, or a pane respawn, each of which re-runs the
registration; there is no command whose purpose is to register a session. Notably `locks advise`
(`internal/cli/locks.go:548-559`) already degrades gracefully instead of failing — it warns and
switches to `--all-agents` scoring — so the graceful pattern exists in the same file.

This is a different defect from the documented `ntm mail` identity bug (`docs/tools/ntm.md`),
which concerns the fixed `HumanOverseer` identity never being created and a URL built from the
tmux session name where the server wants the project slug. That one is about a self-registering
inline identity and a wrong URL; this one is about the per-session coordinator identity that is
supposed to exist from spawn time and does not, with no self-healing anywhere in the lock path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn a swarm: `ntm spawn <project> --label <label> --pi=2:<model>`.
2. Let the pane agents reserve files through Agent Mail, or reserve some by any means that goes
   through a pane identity. Confirm with `ntm locks list <project> --all-agents` that
   reservations exist.
3. As the operator, attempt to reserve a path:
   `ntm lock <project>--<label> "<some/path>" --reason "x" --ttl 10m`.
4. Observe `Error: session '<project>--<label>' has no Agent Mail identity`.
5. Attempt to release: `ntm unlock <project>--<label> --all`. Observe the same error.
6. Confirm the asymmetry: `ntm locks list <project> --all-agents` still succeeds and prints the
   reservations the operator cannot touch.
7. Confirm the file is genuinely absent:
   `ls ~/.config/ntm/sessions/<session>/<projectSlug>/agent.json`.

Reproducing the *original* registration failure is the part not established — see below.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `agent.json` absent for a session that has live reservations, `ntm unlock <session>`
      and `ntm locks force-release` either succeed or fail with an error naming a specific
      command that repairs the situation. A bare "has no Agent Mail identity" with no next step
      is not acceptable.
- [ ] The lock-family commands resolve an identity through the same fallback chain the mail
      commands use, or a documented subset of it: an explicit `--agent` flag at minimum.
- [ ] There is one command whose stated purpose is to create or repair a session's coordinator
      identity, rather than that only happening as a side effect of `add`, `adopt` or a respawn.
- [ ] `RegisterSessionAgent` failing at spawn is reported in `--json` output, not only on the
      human path. A spawn that produced no coordinator identity does not report unqualified
      success.
- [ ] The registration failure is retried or reconciled at least once, matching what
      `registerSpawnedAgents` already does for pane identities.
- [ ] `ntm locks list` continues to work with no identity present, unchanged.
- [ ] Done when: an operator who spawned a swarm, watched its agents reserve files, and then lost
      the swarm can release every one of those reservations with a single documented command.

## Tests

- **Unit test** — `runLock` and `runUnlock` with `loadResolvedSessionAgent` returning nil and an
  `--agent` value supplied: assert the command proceeds using the supplied identity instead of
  erroring.
- **Unit test** — the same two with no identity and no `--agent`: assert the error text names the
  repair command, and assert on that text so a future reword cannot silently drop it.
- **Unit test** — `RegisterSessionAgent` returning a transient/busy error: assert the reconcile
  path runs and the identity ends up present, mirroring the existing coverage shape for
  `registerSpawnedAgents`.
- **Unit test** — spawn under `--json` with `RegisterSessionAgent` failing: assert the JSON
  response carries the failure rather than reporting clean success.
- **End-to-end test** — against a real Agent Mail server: register pane identities, delete the
  session `agent.json` from disk, then release a reservation as the operator and assert it is
  gone from `locks list`. This is the case the unit tests cannot cover, because the defect is a
  disagreement between two stores.

Each new assertion must be driven red on purpose before it is trusted.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/lock.go`, `internal/cli/unlock.go`, the two identity call sites in
`internal/cli/locks.go` (`force-release` and `renew`), `internal/agentmail/session.go` for the
retry, and the registration call site in `internal/cli/spawn.go`. The identity-resolution helper
in `internal/cli/mail.go` is read and possibly shared, not rewritten. The Agent Mail wire
protocol and the reservation schema are not touched, and `locks list` keeps its current
no-identity behaviour.

## Recovery path

The change is to CLI behaviour and to one local JSON file's creation, with no data migration and
no server-side state. Reverting the commit restores the previous refusal; any `agent.json`
written in the meantime is a file the previous code already knew how to read, so no cleanup is
required. If a new repair command proves wrong, deleting the file by hand returns a session to
the state this bead describes.
close_reason: Implemented in ac6953e4. lock/unlock/locks force-release/locks renew resolve an identity through the mail chain (--agent, TMUX_PANE, agent.json, AGENT_NAME); the refusal now names 'ntm mail register <session>', which is a new command that creates or repairs the coordinator identity. RegisterSessionAgent reconciles a transient-busy failure the way registerSpawnedAgents already did, and the spawn --json envelope carries coordinator_identity. locks list unchanged. Six unit tests, each proven red by mutating the branch it targets. NOT done: the end-to-end test against a real Agent Mail server, which is the disagreement between two stores that unit tests cannot reach.

title: A stale error string in the scrollback classifies a working pane as error
description:
## Outcome

A pane that is actively producing output is not classified `error` because of a string left in
its scrollback minutes ago. An error match only wins while it is the pane's *current* state, so
the surfaces that act on `error` — dispatch gating, health restarts, `ntm wait` — stop acting on
a pane that is working.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn an agent pane and let it produce a transient error line — an expired-credential
   message, or a Go binary printing `Error: context canceled` from a bare `ctx.Err()`.
2. Let the agent recover and keep working: the pane is generating output and spending tokens.
3. Read the pane's state through any robot/coordinator surface.
4. The pane reports `state:error` while it is demonstrably working, and keeps reporting it for
   as long as the offending line stays inside the capture window.

Observed on 2026-08-22 with `ctx.Err()` and `invalid_api_key` in the scrollback of healthy,
token-spending panes.

## Context

There are **two independent classifiers**, both driven purely by captured pane *text* — neither
reads a process or exit-status signal:

- `determineStateAt`, `internal/status/unified.go:106`, producing `status.AgentState`
  (`idle`/`working`/`error`/`unknown`, `internal/status/types.go:14-23`).
- `StateClassifier.Classify`, `internal/robot/activity.go:892`, producing `robot.AgentState`
  (`internal/robot/patterns.go:24-25`), used by the coordinator, health and dispatch surfaces.

Each carries its own error table: `errorPatterns` at `internal/status/errors.go:29-84` — the
credential regex at `:45` matches `invalid_api_key`, and a generic `(?im)^error:` prefix at
`:88` catches any line starting `Error:`, including `Error: context canceled` — and a parallel
table at `internal/robot/patterns.go:155` (`invalid_key`) and `:167` (`api_error`).

**The defect is not the patterns. It is where they are allowed to match, and what a match
outranks.**

- `classifyInternal` (`internal/robot/activity.go:928`) runs the pattern match over the **full**
  captured buffer — `LinesStatusDetection = 20` lines
  (`internal/tmux/capture_helpers.go:26`) — separately from the smaller live tail it computes at
  `internal/robot/activity.go:945`.
- `classifyState` (`internal/robot/activity.go:1218-1220`) gives `CategoryError` **absolute
  priority** at confidence 0.95.
- `applyHysteresis` (`internal/robot/activity.go:1279-1290`) lets `StateError` transition
  **immediately**, with no debounce — every other transition is damped.
- The one guard against a stale match, `filterErrorToLiveWhenIdle`
  (`internal/robot/activity.go:1162`), strips the stale error from the full buffer **only when
  the live tail currently shows a fresh idle prompt** (`hasLiveIdle`, `:1176-1181`). When the
  pane is *not* idle — that is, precisely when it is working — the guard no-ops and returns the
  full buffer unchanged (`:1181-1182`).

So the guard covers the harmless case and misses the harmful one. A pane that has gone quiet is
protected; a pane that is busy is not.

The scan scope is bounded in both classifiers and is not the problem to fix: the robot path
captures 20 lines, and `status.DetectErrorInOutput` re-scans the last 50
(`internal/status/errors.go:97-99`, `ScanLines = 50` from `DefaultConfig()`,
`internal/status/detector.go:23`).

**Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug: the consumers act, and one of them is
destructive.**

- `internal/coordinator/monitor.go:110-114` and `:151-155` — overrides the static detector and
  clears `SafeToDispatch`, so a working pane stops receiving work.
- `internal/robot/health.go:604-605` — `checkErrors` / stall detection feeding `RestartManager`
  (`internal/robot/health.go:1646-1750`).
- `internal/robot/diagnose.go:650` — the `ntm diagnose --restart` path.
- `internal/cli/wait.go:239-242` — `ntm wait` fails with `WaitErrorStateError`.
- `internal/coordinator/coordinator.go:775` — emits an `agent.error` event.

A restart of a pane that was merely displaying old text discards whatever that agent had in
context. That is the failure mode this bead exists to remove, and it is the reason the fix must
not simply lengthen the debounce.

An operator-side note that should not be mistaken for the fix: readers already know a pane's
`error` is sniffed from visible text and has to be corroborated before acting. This bead removes
the need for that corroboration in the common case; it does not make `error` a certainty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An error pattern matching **outside** the live tail does not by itself produce `error`
      while the pane shows evidence of progress (output growth between two captures)
- [ ] The same pattern matching **inside** the live tail still produces `error` immediately, with
      today's confidence and today's lack of debounce
- [ ] `filterErrorToLiveWhenIdle` (`internal/robot/activity.go:1162`) — or its replacement —
      covers the working case as well as the idle one, and its name and comment say which cases
      it covers
- [ ] The static classifier at `internal/status/unified.go:106` reaches the same verdict as the
      robot classifier for identical input, or the divergence is documented in a comment naming
      why two answers are correct
- [ ] No consumer changes behaviour for a pane that is genuinely in error: dispatch gating,
      health restart, `ntm diagnose --restart`, `ntm wait` and the `agent.error` event all still
      fire on a real error
- [ ] Classification cost does not grow: no additional tmux capture per classification, and the
      scan window stays at 20 lines for the robot path and 50 for the static one
- [ ] Done when: a fixture pane whose buffer contains `invalid_api_key` five lines back and
      whose tail is actively growing classifies as working, and the same buffer with the match
      in the tail classifies as error.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven with fixture scrollback strings, in the convention of
`internal/status/errors_test.go` (`TestDetectErrorInOutput_*`), `internal/status/unified_test.go`
and `internal/robot/patterns.go`'s own test neighbours. One case per row:

- error string in the live tail, pane idle → `error`
- error string in the live tail, pane working → `error`
- error string outside the live tail, pane idle → not `error` (today's guard, must not regress)
- error string outside the live tail, pane working → **not** `error` (the defect)
- `Error: context canceled` outside the tail, pane working → not `error`
- no error string anywhere → unchanged
- two consecutive captures with no growth and a stale error → `error` (a genuinely stuck pane is
  still caught)

Plus a **regression test asserting hysteresis is unchanged** for every non-error transition
(`internal/robot/activity.go:1279-1290`), so a fix to the error path does not quietly damp the
others.

## Blast radius

`internal/robot/activity.go` — `classifyInternal` (928), `classifyState` (1218-1220),
`applyHysteresis` (1279-1290) and `filterErrorToLiveWhenIdle` (1162-1182) — and, if the two
classifiers are reconciled, `internal/status/unified.go:106`. The error pattern tables
(`internal/status/errors.go:29-88`, `internal/robot/patterns.go:155-167`) are **not** edited:
the strings are right, the placement rule is wrong. No consumer is modified; every one of the
five listed above keeps its current behaviour on a real error.
