title: Health reports a working pane unhealthy from a stale scrollback error
description:
## Outcome

`--robot-health=<session>` stops reporting a working pane as `unhealthy` because of an error
string left in its scrollback minutes ago. The health surface reaches the same verdict about a
recovered pane as the classifier the coordinator uses, so an orchestrator reading health is not
told to worry about a pane that is fine.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run an agent pane and let it emit a transient error line — `connection reset`, or a Go binary
   printing `panic:` — then let it recover and keep producing output.
2. Run `ntm --robot-health=<session>` while the pane is working.
3. The pane reports `"health": "unhealthy"` with reason `error detected: …`, for as long as the
   line stays inside the 50-line scan window.

Established by reading the code on 2026-08-24, in the review of `bd-j5cdo`.

## Context

`bd-j5cdo` fixed the robot `StateClassifier`: an error matching outside the live tail no longer
produces `error` while the pane is progressing. **`internal/robot/health.go` has its own,
third error detector that the fix does not reach.**

`checkErrors` (`internal/robot/health.go:623-690`) does its own capture —
`tmux.CapturePaneOutputContext(ctx, paneID, 50)` at `:633` — and a plain `strings.Contains` scan
against `healthErrorPatterns` (`:422-449`). There is no live-tail window and no progress gating.
`HasErrors` (`:655-657`) becomes `HealthUnhealthy` in `calculateHealthState` (`:751`, reason
`"error detected: "`), and that reaches `GetSessionHealth` (`:895`) and the
`--robot-health=SESSION` JSON envelope (`:949-955`).

The asymmetry is inside this one file and is worth stating plainly: **stall detection is guarded
and error detection is not.** `checkStallWithActivity` (`:569-616`) builds a real
`NewStateClassifier` (`:577-580`) and calls `Classify()` (`:583`), so it inherits the live-tail
and progress logic. `checkErrors` next door does none of that.

**What this costs, and what it does not.** Traced end to end on 2026-08-24, because an earlier
review assumed worse:

- The verdict is **display and alerting only**. Nothing restarts a pane because of it.
- `AutoRestartUnhealthyAgent` (`:2189-2224`) is the one function gated on `HealthUnhealthy` that
  would restart, through `RestartManager.TryRestart` (`:2222-2223`) — and it has **no production
  caller anywhere in the tree**. It is unreachable code, which is the `WS2: wire or delete`
  epic's business, not this bead's.
- `--robot-health-restart-stuck` does restart panes, but `ClassifyStuckPanes` (`:2285-2317`) gates
  on `IdleSinceSeconds` and consults `Health` only to *exclude* `blocked` and `rate_limited`; an
  `unhealthy` pane is treated exactly like a healthy one. So the stale error neither causes nor
  prevents that restart.
- The continuous restart loop in `internal/resilience/monitor.go` is a different system on a
  different package (`internal/health`), which does not import `internal/robot` at all.

So the harm is a false `unhealthy` in a JSON surface an orchestrator reads — not a destroyed
agent context. That is why this is P3 and separate from `bd-j5cdo`, whose blast radius explicitly
excluded the pattern tables.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An error pattern matching outside the live tail does not by itself produce
      `HealthUnhealthy` while the pane shows output growth between two captures
- [ ] The same pattern matching inside the live tail still produces `HealthUnhealthy` with today's
      reason text
- [ ] A pane with a stale error and no output growth still reports `unhealthy` — a genuinely stuck
      pane is not rescued by this change
- [ ] `checkErrors` (`internal/robot/health.go:623-690`) and `checkStallWithActivity` (`:569-616`)
      reach their verdicts through the same guard, or the code says why two answers are correct
- [ ] `healthErrorPatterns` (`:422-449`) is not edited: the strings are right, the placement rule
      is what is wrong
- [ ] No additional tmux capture per health check — `checkErrors` already captures 50 lines at
      `:633` and `checkStallWithActivity` already classifies; the guard reuses what is captured
- [ ] `--robot-health-restart-stuck` classification is unchanged: it gates on idle time, and this
      bead must not make an `unhealthy` verdict start or stop mattering there
- [ ] Done when: a fixture pane whose buffer holds `connection reset` forty lines back and whose
      tail is growing reports `healthy`, and the same buffer with the match in the tail reports
      `unhealthy`.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven with fixture scrollback strings, in the convention of
`internal/robot/health_test.go` (see `calculateHealthState` cases at `health_test.go:100-230`):

- error string in the live tail, pane progressing → `unhealthy`
- error string outside the live tail, pane progressing → **not** `unhealthy` (the defect)
- error string outside the live tail, no growth → `unhealthy` (the stuck pane)
- no error string anywhere → unchanged
- `panic:` and `connection reset` each covered, since they take different branches in
  `healthErrorPatterns`

**Regression test** that `ClassifyStuckPanes` (`:2285-2317`) treats the same fixtures exactly as
it does today, so a change to the health verdict does not silently change which panes are
restartable.

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is where a pattern is allowed to match.

## Blast radius

`internal/robot/health.go` — `checkErrors` (`:623-690`) and, if the two are reconciled, its
relationship to `checkStallWithActivity` (`:569-616`). `healthErrorPatterns` (`:422-449`),
`calculateHealthState` (`:741-760`), the restart machinery (`:1678+`) and the stuck-pane
classifier (`:2285-2317`) are **read, not changed**. Nothing outside this file is touched, and no
other classifier is involved.
close_reason: Implemented in cfd84924. checkErrors now shares the StateClassifier with checkStallWithActivity and applies the same live-tail plus progress guard to healthErrorPatterns: a match outside the live tail is dropped while the pane is progressing or parked at a fresh idle prompt, and kept when it is stuck. healthErrorPatterns unchanged, no extra tmux capture, ClassifyStuckPanes untouched. Verified by mutation in both directions: removing the guard turns three recovered-pane cases red, and making it always drop turns the two stuck-pane cases red, so the fix cannot be loosened or tightened without a test failing. internal/robot green.

title: Bound the forward window in pi session discovery so a pane with no transcript reports no id
description:
## Outcome

A `pi` pane whose own transcript has not been written yet reports **no** `agent_session_id`,
instead of being handed the session id of a pane that started after it. `newestPiSessionForCwdContext`
applies the same bounded start window every other provider's selection already applies, so the
absence of a transcript resolves to absence rather than to a wrong id.

## Context

`bd-f6e` (closed, PR #15) added pi discovery. Its selection rule is: read every `.jsonl` under
`~/.pi/agent/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/`, keep the ones whose header `cwd` matches and that are not
already claimed, sort them by header `startedAt` ascending, and return the **first candidate whose
`startedAt >= processStartedAt`** (`internal/agentsession/discover.go:1085-1147`, the loop at
`:1131-1139`).

That comparison rules out a session that started **before** the pane's process. Nothing rules out
one that started arbitrarily long **after** it. So for a pane whose own transcript does not exist
yet — the pi process is up, the composer is drawn, but the session file has not been appended to —
the earliest qualifying candidate is the *next* pane's session, and that id is returned as if it
were the pane's own.

**Every other provider in this file bounds that side.** Gemini's `newestGeminiSessionForCwdContext`
(`discover.go:1390-1440`) selects through `processStartDelta` (`discover.go:487-496`), which returns
`ok=false` both when `sessionStartedAt < processStartedAt` (`:491-493`) **and** when the delta
exceeds `processSessionWindow`, 5 minutes (`discover.go:49`, `:495`). The pi path calls neither
`processStartDelta` nor anything else that caps the forward delta. This is the one asymmetry
between the two selectors; the rest of pi's shape (claimed record, cwd match, header-derived start)
follows Gemini's.

This matters because of what consumes the field. `bd-4gw` put `agent_session_id` on
`--robot-is-working --session-id` so a consumer can join a bead to the transcript a pane actually
wrote. A wrong id does not fail that join — it succeeds against the wrong file, and the wrong file
is another agent's work. `bd-f6e`'s own fifth acceptance criterion states the principle in the same
words: *"A `pi` pane whose transcript cannot be identified reports no `agent_session_id` at all,
rather than the newest file in the directory. A wrong id is worse than an absent one, because the
consumer joins on it."* The window is what makes that criterion true in the case where the pane's
file is merely late rather than missing forever.

**Why `bd-f6e` did not catch it.** Its six-pane test plants all six transcripts before querying, so
every pane's own file is present and the earliest qualifying candidate is always its own. The gap
is the case where a file is *not yet* there, which no fixture in that test constructs.

**Not a defect of the claimed record.** `claimedSessions` (`discover.go:162`, claimed at `:364-372`)
prevents two panes reporting the *same* id in one capture. It cannot help here: the id handed out
is unclaimed and belongs to a real session — just not to the pane that asked. Claiming it then also
denies it to the pane that owns it, which is the second-order cost.

Claude Code's own selector (`discoverClaudeContext` → `newestFileWithExtContext`,
`discover.go:878-898`, `:1155-1182`) takes the newest file by mtime with no process-start input at
all. That is a separate question with its own upstream process-tree stage in front of it
(`discover.go:219-233`), and it is **out of scope here** — this bead changes the pi path only.

## Steps to Reproduce

Needs no tmux; a temp `HOME` and two planted headers reproduce it, which is also the shape of the
regression test this bead owes.

1. Create `<tmpHome>/.pi/agent/sessions/<PiProjectDir(cwd)>/` for some working directory `cwd`.
2. Plant **one** session file whose header carries `cwd` and a `startedAt` of `T + 300000` ms — five
   minutes after the pane's process start `T`. Do **not** plant a file for the pane under query.
3. Call `Discoverer.DiscoverContext(ctx, "pi", cwd)` for a pane whose process start is `T`.

**Expected:** `nil` — the pane's own transcript does not exist, so there is nothing to report.

**Observed:** the planted session is returned; `SessionID` and `SourcePath` name a file that belongs
to a different pane's run.

The same thing on a live machine: start one pi pane, wait for its composer, start a second pi pane
in the same directory and let only the second one write a first message, then run
`ntm --robot-is-working --session-id`. The first pane reports the second pane's id.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `newestPiSessionForCwdContext` rejects a candidate whose header `startedAt` exceeds
      `processStartedAt` by more than `processSessionWindow` (5 minutes), reusing `processStartDelta`
      rather than a second copy of the comparison
- [ ] A pi pane with no transcript of its own and one later-started sibling transcript in the same
      directory reports **no** `agent_session_id` — not the sibling's
- [ ] The six-pane ordered-assignment case of `bd-f6e` still passes: those transcripts are written
      within milliseconds of their processes, so a 5-minute window must not disturb them
- [ ] The behaviour with no process start time (`processStartedAt <= 0`) is unchanged — newest
      header wins, as today at `discover.go:1141-1146`
- [ ] Done when: a pane whose own transcript is absent reports nothing, proven by a test that fails
      against today's code.

## Tests

- **Unit (Go, `internal/agentsession`):** the reproduction above — one planted transcript five
  minutes ahead of the queried pane's process start, asserting `nil`. This is the test that fails
  without the fix, and it is the one that matters.
- **Unit (Go):** a boundary pair — a candidate just inside the window and one just outside it —
  asserted against literal millisecond values rather than against `processSessionWindow` restated in
  the test, so a change to the constant is visible as a failing test rather than absorbed silently.
- **Unit (Go), regression:** `TestDiscoverPiOrderedAssignment` unchanged and still green, proving the
  window does not break the dense six-pane case it was written for.

## Blast radius

One function in one file: `newestPiSessionForCwdContext` in `internal/agentsession/discover.go`,
plus its tests in `internal/agentsession/agentsession_test.go`. `processStartDelta` is reused as-is
and not modified. No other provider's path, no flag, no schema, no robot surface.
close_reason: verified at 5ec9f284: make build green, go test -short green on ./internal/agentsession/... (the only package touched). PR #23 merged.

title: go test ./... kills the operator's tmux server
description:
## Outcome

`go test ./...` cannot terminate a tmux server the test run did not start. The isolation that
exists today is enforced rather than assumed: a run whose isolation fails skips or fails the
affected test instead of falling back to the host's default socket, and a decoy session on the
socket the test process would otherwise reach survives a full-suite run.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a tmux session on the default socket, attached, named the way an ordinary session is
   named (`0`).
2. From the repository root, run the whole suite against the real environment:
   `HOME=/home/gabriel go test ./... -count=1`
3. The session is gone, along with every pane in it. Observed 2026-08-28 at commit `4e71a9bb`;
   the run was killed with it, so no test output survived to say which package was executing.

A single-package run of `./internal/robot/` does not do it — that package's `TestMain` calls
`testutil.IsolateTmuxTestProcess` (`internal/robot/robot_test.go:152-157`).

**A safe reproduction exists and should be used instead of the destructive one.** Point the test
process at a socket root of its own and put the decoy there, so "the default socket" for that
process is not the operator's: `export TMUX_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)`, start `tmux new-session -d -s
decoy` under it, then run the suite from that shell and check whether `decoy` outlives it. This
reproduces the class of failure — a kill that escapes its intended scope — without betting the
operator's session on it.

## Context

This is the second time the suite has damaged the machine it ran on. On 2026-08-21 it deleted
the real `~/.config`, twice (upstream issue #258, fixed locally in `0a62cd65`). On 2026-08-28 it
killed the live tmux server. The `~/.config` fix held — that directory survived this run — so the
lesson is not that one bug remains open but that the suite reaches the host through more than one
door, and closing them one incident at a time is what has been happening.

**What was ruled out.** In a default run (no build tags) only two test files invoke a raw
`kill-server`, and both are scoped on paper:

- `internal/cli/bind_test.go:741-746` starts and kills its server with an explicit `-L <socket>`,
  which is the containment this bead wants everywhere.
- `internal/tmux/session_test.go:81-100` kills through `cmd.Env` carrying an isolated
  `TMUX_TMPDIR` (`:118-130`).

The two files that kill on the *default* socket via `tmux.NewClient("")` —
`internal/pipeline/real_tmux_integration_test.go:382` and
`internal/tui/dashboard/real_tmux_integration_test.go:33` — both carry `//go:build integration`
and therefore did not compile into this run. They are still worth changing, because their
containment is a process-wide `t.Setenv("TMUX_TMPDIR", ...)` and nothing else.

**So the escape is in the isolation mechanism, not in an unscoped call.** `internal/tmux` never
passes `-L` or `-S`: every `Client` is `DefaultClient` and the only thing separating a test server
from the operator's is the `TMUX_TMPDIR` environment variable
(`internal/tmux/session.go:3031-3039` for `KillSession`, and the client construction around it).
An environment variable is a single point of failure shared by the whole process, and
`bd-9oo` already closed one way it fails: an ambient `NTM_TEST_TMUX_ENV_OWNED=1` made
`IsolateTmuxTestProcess` skip isolation entirely (`tests/testutil/throttle.go:243-252`). That
variable was **not** set in the 2026-08-28 environment, so this is a second route to the same
place rather than a regression of that fix.

Two candidates remain and the repro above is what separates them. First,
`tests/testutil/tmuxenv/sweep.go` — merged the evening before the incident, in PR #34
(`62995487`, "reap tmux test roots an interrupted run left behind") — globs `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`
and `os.TempDir()` for `ntm-tmux-test-*` and runs `kill-server` against each root whose owner pid
is dead (`sweep.go:122-134`), and a comment at `sweep.go:83-86` records an earlier version of the
same sweep reaping 1528 roots from the machine's real temp directories. Second, a package with no
`TestMain` isolation at all reaching the default socket through `tmux.CreateSession` /
`tmux.KillSession` — `internal/pipeline/pipeline_test.go:74-86` is that shape, though it only
names sessions it created.

**The reason a per-incident fix is not enough.** Nothing in `go test`'s output distinguishes a
package that touched only `t.TempDir()` from one that reached the host, and the failure is
discovered by losing something. The operator's standing instruction is now to never run this
suite on this machine, which means the suite is not the safety net it is supposed to be.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every tmux command issued from test code addresses an explicit socket — `-L` or `-S` — so
      containment survives an environment variable being unset, overwritten, or inherited
      wrongly. `internal/cli/bind_test.go:741` is the pattern to copy.
- [ ] A test that cannot establish its own socket **skips or fails**; no code path falls back to
      the default socket. Verified by forcing the isolation to fail and observing the skip.
- [ ] `tests/testutil/tmuxenv/sweep.go` kills nothing outside a root this run created: the owner
      marker is verified before the kill, not only globbed for.
- [ ] The safe reproduction above runs the full suite with a decoy session in place and the decoy
      is alive afterwards, in three consecutive runs.
- [ ] A guard test fails if a new `kill-server` or `kill-session` call appears in test code
      without an explicit socket flag, so this does not have to be caught by losing a session a
      third time.
- [ ] Done when: `go test ./...` can be run on a machine with live tmux sessions and none of them
      is affected.

## Tests

- Unit, over `tests/testutil/tmuxenv`: a root whose owner pid is alive is not reaped; a root
  outside the run's own base is not matched.
- Integration, over the harness itself: with isolation deliberately broken (unset the variable the
  helper depends on), the affected tests skip rather than proceeding against the default socket.
- Unit, as a static guard — a test that greps the tree for `kill-server` / `kill-session` in `*_test.go`
  and fails on any occurrence without `-L`/`-S`. It is the only one of the three that keeps
  working when someone adds a new tmux test.

## Blast radius

Test scaffolding only: `tests/testutil/throttle.go`, `tests/testutil/tmuxenv/`,
`internal/tmux/session_test.go`, and the two `real_tmux_integration_test.go` files under
`internal/pipeline` and `internal/tui/dashboard`. Production code is not touched — `internal/tmux`
gains no new API unless the fix chooses to pass a socket through `Client`, in which case that
change and its callers belong to this bead too and the field is additive.

## Recovery path

The change is confined to test code, so reverting the commit restores the previous behaviour and
nothing outside the test binaries is affected. The operator's containment in the meantime is to
run only the packages a change touched, never the tree.
close_reason: Verified in a container: decoy killed at 4e71a9bb (before the fix), survived three consecutive full-suite runs at 433077d2. Shipped in PR #36 (explicit socket on Client, killing call sites named, repo-wide ratchet guard) and PR #37 (scripts/test-in-container.sh, the safe way to verify this). The kill is a cross-package interaction under go test's parallelism, not one call site: bisected package by package on the pre-fix tree, every package's decoy survived alone. See the final comment for the evidence and for what was left open.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text:
Second incident, 2026-08-28 02:38, and it moves the diagnosis.

The suite was run twice under containment: a `tmux` wrapper installed on `PATH` and via
`NTM_TMUX_BINARY` that forces `-S <private socket>` onto any invocation not already naming
one, a private `TMUX_TMPDIR`, and decoy sessions on that private socket.

Run 1, on the branch carrying the fix: both decoys alive afterwards, operator's session
untouched. Run 2, the control on `main` without the fix: the operator's live tmux server died
again, taking the session with it.

The control was a mistake to run — the containment had a known hole at the time it was
started, and the hole is what let the kill through. The hole is worth recording because it is
also a finding about the code: `tests/testutil/throttle.go:327` (`findSystemTmuxBinary`) and
`internal/tmux`'s equivalent resolve `/usr/bin/tmux` by absolute path and deliberately ignore
`NTM_TMUX_BINARY`, so no wrapper and no `PATH` manipulation can intercept them. Any containment
built on substituting the binary is therefore incomplete by construction, and that is worth
knowing before anyone else tries to verify this bead the same way.

**What the evidence rules out.** The private socket ended the control run holding both decoys
and three leaked test sessions, and the wrapper's log recorded exactly two `kill-server`
invocations across 10,187 tmux calls — both carrying `-L`, both from `internal/cli/bind_test.go`,
which is the correctly scoped one. So no blind `kill-server` was issued through any path the
wrapper could see. Whatever killed the default server either used an absolute binary path, or
was not a tmux command at all.

**Two candidates the original analysis did not carry**, both reachable from an untagged
`go test ./...`:

- `tests/testutil/tmux_lock_unix.go:158,206,227` — `syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` against a
  "guardian" process group. A wrong or zero pgid signals the caller's own group, which in an
  interactive session is everything sharing that group.
- `internal/cli/monitor_integration_test.go:50,234,349` — `pkill -f <pattern>`. The pattern is
  built to be anchored, but a `pkill` reaching outside the test's own processes leaves exactly
  this signature: the server dies with nothing in any tmux log.

Neither is a tmux command, which is consistent with the wrapper seeing nothing. The acceptance
criterion about an explicit socket remains right and remains necessary; it is now clear it is
not sufficient, and the bead should not be closed on the strength of the socket work alone.

**How to verify this bead from here, without betting a session on it:** run the suite from a
machine state where there is no session worth losing — a second tmux server started for the
purpose and nothing else attached, or a container. Substituting the tmux binary is not
containment, for the reason above.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text:
Verified in a container, with the control the earlier attempts lacked. All four runs were the
full suite, each with a decoy session on the container's own default socket.

| run | tree | decoy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `4e71a9bb`, before the socket fix | killed |
| B1 | `433077d2`, fix merged | survived |
| B2 | same | survived |
| B3 | same | survived |

That is the acceptance criterion asking for three consecutive clean runs, plus the negative
control proving the same suite still kills without the fix. It also corrects the reading in the
previous comment: the instrumented host run saw no blind `kill-server` and I concluded the cause
was not a tmux command. It was — the killing paths resolve `/usr/bin/tmux` by absolute path, so
they were invisible to an instrument that worked by substituting the binary. Absent from the log
is not absent from the run.

**The kill is an interaction between packages, not a single call site.** Bisecting the pre-fix
tree package by package, each run with its own decoy, produced `DECOY SURVIVED` for every one of
`tests/testutil/...`, `internal/tmux/...`, `internal/checkpoint/...`, `internal/resilience/...`
and `internal/cli/...` — including the two that own the isolation machinery. `go test ./...` runs
packages in parallel, so a kill issued against the shared default socket by one package takes
down the server another package started, and the decoy with it. Run alone, each package's kill
finds only its own server and looks correct. That is why every single-package reproduction
attempt came back clean, on the host and here, and it is the argument for the fix being an
explicit socket per client rather than a correction to one caller.

**What shipped.** PR #36: `Client.Socket` plus `NewClientWithSocket`, `-S` prefixed ahead of the
subcommand, the killing call sites in `tests/testutil`, `internal/tmux`'s `TestMain` and the two
`//go:build integration` cleanups all naming their socket, and a repo-wide ratchet guard that
fails on a new unsocketed `kill-server`/`kill-session`/`new-session` while tolerating a
per-file snapshot of the ~120 that already existed. PR #37: `scripts/test-in-container.sh` and
`test.Containerfile`, which is how this bead was verified and how the next person should verify
anything in this suite.

**Left open deliberately, and each deserves its own bead if anyone wants it.** The ~120 legacy
call sites still address the default socket and are held only by their packages' `TestMain`
isolation. Eleven packages fail inside the container for environment reasons — tmux 3.5a there
against 3.7b on the host, no `br`/`bv`, no network — which is noise this bead never promised to
clear. And the suite still leaks tmux sessions it created; three were left behind on the private
socket during one run.

title: Add a pi case to needsBufferSend so multi-line prompts reach pi panes intact
description:
## Outcome

`needsBufferSend` returns true for a pi pane whose content contains a newline, so `ntm assign` and `ntm send` deliver a multi-line prompt to pi through a tmux buffer rather than through `send-keys -l`. A prompt written in paragraphs arrives at a pi composer with its line breaks intact, and the words on either side of a break are no longer joined into one.

## Context

`needsBufferSend` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2081-2111`) decides delivery per agent type. It has three cases — `AgentClaude` (2087-2099), `AgentGemini`/`AgentAntigravity` (2100-2103), `AgentCodex` (2104-2107) — and a `default: return false` (2108-2110). Of the thirteen agent types declared in `internal/agent/types.go:16-28`, **nine** reach that default unconditionally, newlines or not: Pi, Grok, Ollama, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, Opencode, User and Unknown.

The function's own comment states the consequence, and it is why the Claude case exists at all: `send-keys -l` loses the newlines, while `paste-buffer` converts them to CR, which a composer reads as Enter. For a pi pane the newline is dropped and **nothing is put in its place**, so the last word of one line is concatenated with the first word of the next.

Measured on tmux 3.7b against a two-paragraph prompt delivered to a pi pane with `send-keys -l`, four joins arrived fused: `{TITLE}This`, `stop.Before`, `afternoon.While`, `string.How`. Every one sits exactly where the source had a line break. The same text delivered through `load-buffer` + `paste-buffer -p` arrives with every break intact, which is the difference this bead closes.

The cost is not hypothetical and is already being paid downstream. The marching-orders prompt template now defends itself against this: its blank lines each hold a single space, and its section titles carry a `##` marker, purely so that a dropped newline still leaves a boundary between two words. That is a workaround living in a prose file for a defect in the delivery code, and it is fragile in a way nothing announces — trailing whitespace is what an editor, a formatter or a pre-commit hook strips by default. Any prompt written by anyone else gets no such protection.

**`AgentUser` and `AgentUnknown` must keep returning false.** A user pane is a shell, where a newline legitimately means Enter and buffer delivery would change the meaning of the input. This is the reason the fix is a pi case rather than a change to the default: the default is correct for the panes that are not agent composers.

**Grok, Ollama, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider and Opencode are equally affected and are deliberately out of scope.** Each needs its own composer observed before its behaviour is changed, and `TestNeedsBufferSend` currently asserts `want: false` for Cursor, Windsurf and Aider in an explicit `default: never uses buffer` block (`internal/tmux/session_test.go:2382-2406`). Flipping those without evidence would replace a deliberate assertion with a guess. Each deserves its own bead once its composer has been checked.

No capability registry exists to express this more generally. Six independent switches on `agentType.Canonical()` each own one concern — `NeedsDoubleEnter` (`internal/agent/types.go:190-204`), `ValidateAutomatedPromptDelivery` (`internal/agent/types.go:171-186`), `needsBufferSend`, `composerMarkerForAgent` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2223-2232`), `composerPlaceholderPrefixes` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2237-2246`) and `classifyComposerDeliveryVerdict` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2359-2382`). Adding a case is the codebase's own pattern, not a shortcut around a missing abstraction; introducing a registry here would be a separate change with a separate justification.

Precedent: `384f91b0` (2026-03-07) added the Claude case in exactly this shape and flipped one `want` in the test table in the same commit. `upstream/main` is ahead by five commits touching `internal/tmux/session.go` and **none of them touches `needsBufferSend`**, so there is no upstream fix to take instead of writing one.

This is the fourth defect of one shape: pi missing from a per-agent switch. See `bd-gc0` (pi panes reported as codex by the robot state surfaces), `bd-g3a` (`detectAgentTypeFromPane` has no pi case) and `bd-ffv3d` (spawn prompt delivery to pi panes). Worth noting when deciding whether the registry is still out of scope after this one.

## Steps to Reproduce

Needs a disposable tmux session; no live pane may be used. Measured against tmux 3.7b.

```sh
# 1. a throwaway two-paragraph prompt whose paragraph boundary is a word pair
printf 'first paragraph ends here.\n\nSecond paragraph starts here.\n' > /tmp/probe.txt

# 2. a disposable pi pane
tmux new-session -d -s bufprobe -x 200 -y 50 'pi'
sleep 12   # wait for the composer footer

# 3. deliver the way needsBufferSend routes a pi pane today
tmux send-keys -t bufprobe -l -- "$(cat /tmp/probe.txt)"
sleep 1; tmux send-keys -t bufprobe Enter; sleep 1; tmux send-keys -t bufprobe Enter
sleep 5; tmux send-keys -t bufprobe Escape

# 4. read the delivered prompt back
tmux capture-pane -p -S -200 -t bufprobe | grep -oE 'here\.Second'
```

**Expected:** no output — the paragraph break survives as a break or at minimum as a space.

**Observed:** `here.Second`. The two paragraphs are welded into one word pair.

Tear down with `tmux kill-session -t bufprobe`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `needsBufferSend` returns `true` for `AgentPi` when the content contains `\n`, and `false` for `AgentPi` when it does not
- [ ] `AgentUser` and `AgentUnknown` still return `false` for multi-line content, asserted by a test case each — the default is correct for a shell pane and this bead must not widen it
- [ ] `TestNeedsBufferSend` (`internal/tmux/session_test.go:2182`) gains a pi-with-newline case and a pi-single-line case in the table's existing struct shape, and the `default: never uses buffer` block at 2382-2406 no longer implies pi
- [ ] Cursor, Windsurf and Aider keep their `want: false` assertions unchanged — this bead changes one agent type
- [ ] `go test ./internal/tmux/ -run TestNeedsBufferSend` passes, and fails if the new pi case is reverted while the test is kept
- [ ] The reproduction above, re-run after the change through `ntm assign`, shows the paragraph break intact in the pane capture and the grep empty
- [ ] Done when: a multi-line prompt dispatched to a pi pane arrives with every line break preserved, verified by reading the pane rather than by an exit code.

## Tests

- **Unit**: table cases added to `TestNeedsBufferSend` — pi with a newline (`want: true`), pi single-line (`want: false`), and the two guard cases for User and Unknown. This is where the regression is cheap to catch.
- **Manual, one-shot, end-to-end**: dispatch a multi-line prompt to a disposable pi pane through `ntm assign` and capture the pane. The unit test proves the routing decision; only the pane proves the bytes arrived, and the defect lives in the gap between the two.
- **Unit, not owed**: a further unit test over the `paste-buffer` path itself. That path is already exercised by the Claude, Gemini and Codex unit cases in the same table, and it is not what changes here.

## Recovery path

Revert the single case. Delivery for pi returns to `send-keys -l`, which is the current behaviour, so the revert degrades rather than breaks. The marching-orders template's own separators remain in place independently and keep that prompt readable either way.

## Blast radius

Two files: `internal/tmux/session.go` (one `case` in one function) and `internal/tmux/session_test.go` (table cases). No other switch is touched, no config key is added, no schema changes, and no other agent type's behaviour changes.

title: Give --robot-rano-stats a session filter
description:
## Outcome

`--robot-rano-stats` accepts `--session` and reports statistics for the panes of that session
only. It is the last robot query that answers about per-session state with no way to say which
session.

## Context

The 2026-08-23 inventory of the 154 registered `--robot-*` flags put eight queries in the bucket
"answers about per-session state, ignores `--session`". Seven of them already filter by a session
flag of their own and only need renaming — that is the convergence bead. **`--robot-rano-stats`
(`internal/cli/root.go:3063`) is the eighth, and the only one with no session filtering of any
kind.** Its only selector is `--panes`, and a pane identifier is not unique across sessions, so
even that selector cannot express "this session's panes" without the caller enumerating them
first.

`--session` is registered on the same flag set as every robot flag (`internal/cli/root.go:4787`),
so passing it here parses cleanly and is then discarded — the same silent-wrong-scope failure
measured on `--robot-status`, with the difference that here there is no filtering machinery to
route it into. This is why it is its own bead rather than a line in the convergence one: the work
is new filtering logic, not a rename.

The resolution path to reuse is the shared one — `resolveRobot…Session`
(`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`) falling back to `robotSharedSession` (`:4787`) — so the flag
plumbing is settled and what this bead owes is the filter underneath it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--robot-rano-stats --session <name>` reports statistics computed only from the panes of
      that session
- [ ] The session is resolved through the shared helper path (`internal/cli/root.go:5387-5401`),
      not through a resolution written for this query
- [ ] With no `--session`, the output is byte-identical to today's — asserted
- [ ] `--panes` and `--session` given together intersect: the named panes, restricted to that
      session, with a pane outside the session reported rather than silently dropped
- [ ] A `--session` naming a session that does not exist returns `success:false` with
      `error_code: SESSION_NOT_FOUND`
- [ ] The scoped answer differs from the unscoped answer whenever a second session has panes —
      the criterion that proves the filter runs
- [ ] Done when: with two live sessions holding panes, `ntm --robot-rano-stats --session <one>`
      counts only that session's panes.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven, over a stubbed pane inventory so no tmux server is needed, in the
style of `internal/cli/robot_session_flag_test.go`:

- scoped to one of two stub sessions → only that session's panes counted
- unscoped → every pane, output unchanged from today (regression)
- `--panes` plus `--session`, all panes inside the session → the named panes
- `--panes` plus `--session`, one pane outside the session → that pane is reported, not dropped
- unknown session → `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`

No fuzz, property or golden tests are owed: the change is one filter over a list.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/root.go` — the `--robot-rano-stats` dispatch branch at `:3063` and the shared
resolution helpers at `:5387-5401` — plus the statistics function it calls in `internal/robot/`,
which gains a session scope. No other robot query, no classifier and no capture path is touched.

title: spawn and add panes carry the launcher's attributable identity env
description:
## Outcome

Every pane created by `ntm spawn` and `ntm add` carries the same attributable identity env the launcher's identity work (bd-fug) established, and its agent-mail registration carries a non-empty task_description — so a tracker claim maps to a pane without archaeology.

## Context

Measured 2026-08-31 shakedown (orchestrator survey, ntm defects and the agent-mail seam): spawn/add panes carried no AGENT_NAME, so claims arrived under agent-mail aliases (BoldHawk, RosePond), raw ntm envelope names, and once as bare "Gabriel"; two of the newest agent registrations had empty task_description, so RosePond/FrostyValley could not be placed on a pane from the store at all. Identity-to-pane mapping was done via sqlite against the agents table plus per-pane scrollback greps plus bead labels as last resort. Every downstream reader — assignee-keyed queries, the held-too-long actor, close attribution — degrades to guesswork when the claim's actor is unmappable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Panes created by `spawn` and by `add` export the identity env (AGENT_NAME or the bd-fug equivalent) with a value that encodes session and pane address, verified by reading the env of a live spawned pane's process.
- [ ] The agent-mail registration made for such a pane carries a non-empty task_description naming session and pane.
- [ ] A claim made from a spawned pane arrives in the tracker with an actor that a documented rule maps back to the pane (the session-prefixed address form swarm-tick already parses).
- [ ] Done when: on a fresh 2-pane spawn, `br list --json` after each pane self-claims shows two distinct pane-mappable assignees and zero aliases.

## Tests

- Integration: spawn a throwaway 2-pane session in the test harness, read the pane processes' env, assert the identity variables; unit: registration payload builder includes task_description.

## Blast radius

Confined to ntm's spawn/add launch path (env assembly and agent-mail registration) and its tests. No tracker schema change; marching-orders templates unchanged (they already consume the identity when present).

title: work queue-dry counts blocked beads as actionable
description:
## Outcome

`ntm work queue-dry` reports as actionable only the beads a tracker would actually hand out, so
its count agrees with `br ready` bead for bead — or it names the reader it used and the filter it
applied, so a caller can tell the two numbers apart on purpose rather than by accident.

## Context

Measured on an eleven-hour unattended swarm against `agent-usage-book` on 2026-08-25/26, a
tracker of 189 beads with a deep dependency chain.

`ntm work queue-dry` reported `ready_count: 5` and `actionable_count: 5` at a moment when the
tracker itself reported nothing ready at all. Among the five it offered was `aub-71j.4`, whose
dependencies are three **open** beads and which `br blocked` lists. So ntm's readiness is a
status filter that does not walk the dependency graph: it counts a bead as ready because its own
status is open, without asking whether anything it depends on is closed.

The consequence is a reporting layer that confidently contradicts the tracker. On this run
nothing was dispatched wrongly, and that was luck rather than design: `bin/swarm-tick` in the
operator's own tooling sources its dispatch row from `br ready --unassigned` and only its
narrative row from ntm, and a second defect — no `pi` pane ever classifying as confidently idle
— meant the dispatch row never fired at all. Two defects cancelled into safety. A consumer that
trusts `queue-dry` for dispatch, which is what the name invites, hands an agent a bead whose
blockers are open.

The operator's workaround was to treat the row as narrative and read `br ready --unassigned` for
every decision, all night. That is a missing feature with its shape already drawn: the count is
only useful if it means what the tracker means.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a repo with a `br` tracker, create bead A and bead B, both open.
2. `br dep add B A` — B now depends on A, which is open.
3. `br ready --json` — B is absent, correctly.
4. `ntm work queue-dry --format=json` from the same repo.
5. Observe B counted in `ready_count` / `actionable_count`, and offered among `triage_top_ids`.

Observed 2026-08-26 with the real tracker: `ntm work queue-dry --format=json` →
`"ready_count": 5, "actionable_count": 5, "triage_top_ids": ["aub-71j.4", ...]` against
`br ready --unassigned` → `✨ No ready issues`, with `br show aub-71j.4 --json` giving
dependencies `[('aub-71j.2','open','blocks'), ('aub-71j.1','open','blocks'),
('aub-vcx.2','open','blocks')]`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given the two-bead reproduction above, `ntm work queue-dry` does not count B as ready or
      actionable, and does not offer it in `triage_top_ids`
- [ ] Given a tracker where `br ready --json` returns N beads, `queue-dry`'s ready count equals N
      and the id sets are identical — checked by comparing the two sets, not the two integers
- [ ] The transitive case holds: C depends on B, B depends on A, A open — neither B nor C is
      counted
- [ ] A bead deferred with `br defer --until <date>` is excluded, matching `br ready`'s own
      definition of ready as open, unblocked and not deferred
- [ ] If the graph cannot be walked for any reason, the output says so and the count is reported
      as unavailable rather than as a number — a status-only fallback that silently reports a
      larger number is the defect itself
- [ ] The JSON shape is unchanged for existing consumers: the same keys, with corrected values
- [ ] Done when: on a tracker whose ready set is empty and whose blocked set is not,
      `ntm work queue-dry --format=json` reports `ready_count: 0`.

## Tests

- **Unit:** over the readiness predicate, with a fixture graph covering direct blockage,
  transitive blockage, a closed blocker (ready), a deferred bead, and a bead with no edges.
- **Integration:** against a real `br` tracker created in the test, asserting set equality
  against `br ready --json` rather than count equality — two different wrong answers can share a
  count.
- **Regression:** the exact shape from the Context, three open blockers on one bead, asserting
  it is absent from `triage_top_ids`.
- **Mutation, before the fix is trusted:** make a blocker closed and confirm the bead appears;
  reopen it and confirm it disappears. A test that only asserts absence passes against a
  `queue-dry` that returns nothing at all.

## Blast radius

The readiness computation behind the `work queue-dry` command and its JSON serialization, plus
the tests for both. No change to the command's flags, its output keys, or any other `ntm work`
sub-verb.

title: Print a readiness verdict per pane at spawn
description:
## Outcome

`ntm spawn` prints one readiness verdict per pane: which classifier decided the pane was ready
to receive its prompt, or that no classifier exists for that agent type and delivery was
allowed unchecked. A run where prompts silently do not arrive is visible in the spawn output
instead of being discovered forty turns later.

## Context

On 2026-08-22 a six-pane swarm lost roughly thirteen minutes and forty turns to prompts that
were never delivered. The post-run survey's own words were that a single line — *"this agent
type has no classifier, prompts were not delivered, send them yourself"* — would have saved the
whole manual-delivery detour. The proximate cause that day was a stale installed binary, but
the reason it cost an hour is that **nothing in the spawn output says whether readiness was
established, guessed, or skipped.**

The delivery gate is `ComposerReadyForDelivery` (`internal/tmux/session.go:2331`, public wrapper
at `:2359`). It resolves a per-type composer marker through `composerMarkerForAgent`
(`internal/tmux/session.go:2203`), and **that table defines exactly two entries** —
`AgentClaude` → `❯` and `AgentCodex` → `›`. For those two it falls back to
`agent.ClaudeActivelyWorking` / `codexLooksWorking`.

**For every other agent type the gate fails open, silently.** The comment at
`internal/tmux/session.go:2326-2328` states it outright: unknown agent types, empty captures and
capture errors all return `ready=true`. Failing open is a defensible default — a gate that
blocks delivery on an unrecognised pane would strand every new agent type — but it is currently
indistinguishable, from the outside, from a pane that was actually checked.

A second path is quieter still: `buildSpawnPromptSequenceForAgent`
(`internal/cli/spawn.go:3938`) returns an **empty step list** for a type whose delivery is not
implemented (`ValidateAutomatedPromptDelivery`, `internal/agent/types.go:181`, which today fails
closed only for Grok — `ErrAutomatedPromptDeliveryNotImplemented`, `internal/agent/types.go:38`
and `:46`). Nothing is printed and spawn exits 0. A pane that will never receive its prompt
looks exactly like a pane that did.

By contrast the **timeout** path is already loud: `waitForSpawnPaneReady`
(`internal/cli/spawn.go:5932`) leads to `"⚠ Warning: spawn prompt delivery failed for agent %d:
%v"` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:3300`), recorded through `recordSetupError` and aggregated after
`setupWg.Wait()` into `"spawn prompt setup failed: …; the session and affected panes still
exist"` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:3440-3443`), with a non-nil error out of `RunE`. So the machinery
for reporting per-pane setup outcomes exists — it just has nothing to say about the two silent
cases.

**What PR #3 already fixed, and what this bead is not.** Commit `d58a18eb` ("Qualify tmux session
targets, and make pi panes classifiable", 2026-08-21, 14 files, 623 insertions) added the `pi`
status-line prompt pattern and the `knownAgentTypes` entries for `pi` and `agy`
(`internal/status/patterns.go`), pi-specific detectors in `internal/agent/patterns.go`, the
wiring in `internal/status/unified.go`, and session-target qualification in
`internal/tmux/session.go` and `internal/resilience/monitor.go`. That fix is merged and the
installed binary now carries it. **This bead does not re-fix pi; it makes the verdict visible
for every type, including the ones nobody has written a classifier for yet.**

Note that the two classifiers are keyed the same way — `agent.AgentType.Canonical()`, which
normalises `claude`→`cc` and `codex`→`cod` — so the verdict line can name the canonical type
without inventing a second vocabulary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ntm spawn` prints exactly one readiness line per pane, naming the pane, the canonical
      agent type, and one of three verdicts: checked-and-ready, no-classifier (delivery allowed
      unchecked), or delivery-not-implemented
- [ ] The no-classifier verdict names what the operator must do — send the prompt by hand — and
      is printed for every type outside the `composerMarkerForAgent` table
      (`internal/tmux/session.go:2203`)
- [ ] A type whose prompt sequence comes back empty from
      `buildSpawnPromptSequenceForAgent` (`internal/cli/spawn.go:3938`) produces the
      delivery-not-implemented verdict rather than silence
- [ ] The existing timeout warning at `internal/cli/spawn.go:3300` and the aggregated error at
      `:3440-3443` keep their current text and their current non-zero exit
- [ ] The gate keeps failing open: no agent type that spawns today starts failing to spawn
      because of this change — the verdict is reporting, never enforcement
- [ ] The verdict lines survive `--robot`/JSON output as a field, not only as human text, so an
      orchestrator can read them
- [ ] Spawning six panes adds no more than one extra tmux capture per pane over today's spawn
- [ ] Done when: spawning a pane of a type with no composer marker prints the no-classifier
      verdict, and spawning `claude` and `codex` panes prints the checked verdict.

## Tests

**Unit tests**, table-driven in the convention of `internal/status/patterns_test.go`
(`TestIsPromptLine` at `:45`, `TestDetectIdleFromOutput` at `:99` — slices of
`{name, line, agentType, expected}` run through `t.Run`). Cases, one per verdict:

- `cc` and `cod` with a composer marker present → checked-and-ready
- a type absent from `composerMarkerForAgent` → no-classifier verdict, and `ready=true`
  unchanged
- an empty capture and a capture error → no-classifier verdict, `ready=true` (the fail-open
  contract, asserted rather than assumed)
- a type whose prompt sequence is empty → delivery-not-implemented verdict
- a readiness timeout → existing warning text, unchanged, and a non-nil error

Plus one **end-to-end** spawn test in the style of `internal/cli/spawn_error_test.go`, injecting
the existing `spawnSessionObserver` / `spawnPromptDispatcher` interfaces (the codebase has no
global fake tmux; those seams are how spawn is tested), asserting one verdict line per pane and
the exit status.

## Blast radius

`internal/cli/spawn.go` — the per-agent block at `3260-3335` and the summary after
`setupWg.Wait()` at `3420-3460`, where per-pane setup outcomes are already assembled — plus a
verdict value returned from or alongside `ComposerReadyForDelivery`
(`internal/tmux/session.go:2331-2359`). `composerMarkerForAgent` and the fail-open behaviour are
**read, not changed**. No change to `internal/status/patterns.go` or to any classifier: this
bead reports what the existing ones decide.
